en: 6  Heritage and Violence
zh: 6  遗产与暴力

en: One of the odd things about the arrival of the era of the modern nationstate was that for a state to prove that it was modern, it helped if it could also prove that it was ancient. A nation that wanted to show that it was upto-date and deserved a place among the company of modern states needed, among other things, to produce a past. This past was not just a piece of symbolic equipment, like a flag or an anthem, with which to organize political allegiance and demonstrate a distinct identity. As many recent studies of nationalism point out, deciding on a common past was critical to the process of making a particular mixture of people into a coherent nation.
zh: 现代民族国家时代到来时，一个奇怪之处在于：一个国家要证明自己是现代的，若能同时证明自己历史悠久，也会大有帮助。一个想表明自己与时俱进、有资格跻身现代国家之列的民族，除其他条件外，还需要制造一个过去。这个过去不只是像国旗或国歌那样的一件象征装备，用来组织政治效忠、展示独特身份。正如晚近许多民族主义研究所指出的，确定一个共同的过去，对于把特定的人群混合体造就成一个连贯的民族这一过程至关重要。

en: The idea of the nation presents a way of living the experience of social relations by imagining them to extend back over a continuous period of time. The political community can then understand its present historically. The projection into the past may help make the present seem natural, disguising some of the arbitrariness, injustice, and coercion on which it depends. Historical thinking achieves this not just by projecting a past, but by organizing that past as the life of a self-directing object, the “nation” or “society.” Contemporary political arrangements acquire a degree of inevitability by appearing as the genetic destiny of this historical being.
zh: 民族的观念提供了一种体验社会关系的方式：把它们想象为在连续的时间中延伸。政治共同体于是可以从历史角度理解自己的现在。向过去的投射可能有助于使现在显得自然，掩饰现在所依赖的某些任意、不公和强制。历史思维实现这一点，不仅靠投射一个过去，还把这个过去组织为一个自我引导的客体——“民族”或“社会”——的生命。当代政治安排通过显得像是这个历史存在的基因命运，获得了一定程度的必然性。

en: Recent writings on nationalism have also pointed out that to produce a past a nation-state had to produce a place. If making the nation depended on extending present social relations back through time, this could only be done by defining their geographical boundaries. Benedict Anderson argues that the idea of the nation came about when modern forms of writing enabled the social worlds of individual citizens to expand. Innovations such as the modern novel and newspaper made it possible for people to imagine unknown others as members of the same community.

Yet in many parts of the world, as Anderson also acknowledges, the idea of the nation required people not only to expand their sense of community in new ways, but in equally novel ways to constrict it. People’s sense of religious community or tribal cognation, their networks of trade and migration, communities of learning and law, and patterns of imperial power and allegiance were in many places much more diverse than the narrow boundaries of modern nation-states. Ernest Renan famously remarked that the idea of the nation required that people learn to forget certain aspects of their past.

Many people also had to learn to forget, or at least to reconsider, their sense of place. They were supposed to reduce the significance of those interconnections, exchanges, genealogies, hegemonies, moral systems, and migrations that defined a social landscape whose horizons reached beyond what became the boundaries of the nation, or even to forget their existence altogether.
zh: 晚近关于民族主义的著作还指出，要制造一个过去，民族国家还必须制造一个地点。如果说造就民族取决于把当下的社会关系向时间深处延伸，那么这只有通过界定其地理边界才能做到。本尼迪克特·安德森认为，民族的观念产生于现代写作形式使个体公民的社会世界得以扩展之时。现代小说和报纸之类的创新，使人们能够把不认识的他人想象为同一共同体的成员。
然而，正如安德森也承认的，在世界许多地方，民族的观念不仅要求人们以新的方式扩展共同体感，还要求人们以同样新颖的方式收缩它。人们的宗教共同体或部落亲缘感，贸易与移民网络，学术与法律共同体，以及帝国权力与效忠的模式，在许多地方都比现代民族国家的狭窄边界更加多样。欧内斯特·勒南有句名言：民族的观念要求人们学会遗忘自己过去的某些方面。
许多人也必须学会遗忘，或至少重新考虑自己的地方感。他们应当降低那些相互联系、交换、谱系、霸权、道德体系和迁徙的重要性——正是这些界定了某种社会景观，其视野超出了后来成为民族边界的范围——甚至要完全忘却它们的存在。

en: Until the late nineteenth century, those in power in Cairo did not consider themselves to be ruling over an object that corresponds to the twentiethcentury nation-state known by the name of Egypt. In the 1930s, a British historian of colonial India popularized the view of Mehmed Ali, the Ottoman governor of Cairo in the first half of the preceding century, as “the founder of modern Egypt.”

Yet Mehmed Ali saw himself as a provincial governor within the Ottoman Empire, not as the ruler of a political entity defined by its geographic body. He undertook a remarkable program of industrialization and military expansion, colonized the Sudan, and took control of Ottoman provinces in Arabia, Palestine, and Syria. As Khaled Fahmy shows, however, these developments were not organized and undertaken as a proto-nationalist project to build a territorially imagined “modern Egypt,” but were an attempt to remake, from the province of Cairo, the Ottoman order.

Politics was imagined and undertaken as a world of expanding imperial authority, not of territorially bounded nation-states. The particular geographic state that began to emerge in the colonial period, it follows, was one of several possible outcomes of this imperial history.
zh: 直到19世纪末，开罗的掌权者都不认为自己统治着一个与20世纪名为埃及的民族国家相对应的客体。1930年代，一位研究殖民地印度的英国历史学家使这样一种看法流行起来：穆罕默德·阿里——19世纪上半叶开罗的奥斯曼总督——是“现代埃及的奠基人”。
然而，穆罕默德·阿里视自己为奥斯曼帝国的一个省总督，而不是一个由其地理躯体所界定的政治实体的统治者。他推行了一项引人注目的工业化和军事扩张计划，殖民苏丹，并控制了奥斯曼帝国在阿拉伯、巴勒斯坦和叙利亚的省份。然而，正如哈立德·法赫米所表明的，这些发展并不是作为一项在领土上想象“现代埃及”的原民族主义工程来组织和实施的，而是试图以开罗省为基点重造奥斯曼秩序。
政治被想象并实践为一个不断扩张的帝国权威的世界，而不是一个领土有限的民族国家的世界。由此可知，殖民时期开始出现的那个特定地理国家，是这段帝国历史的若干可能结果之一。

en: The relatively recent formation of the national state is obscured by the English words routinely used to translate Arabic place-names from the nineteenth century. Ottoman provinces were generally referred to by the name of the city that ruled them.

Mehmed Ali was the governor of the province of Misr, or Cairo. The term suggested not the city alone but the city and its country, meaning the hinterland of towns and villages that supported it, politically and materially. This meaning was also invoked with phrases such as “the Cairo region” and “Cairo country.”

From the later nineteenth century, however, the word Cairo (misr) also came to be used by extension to describe a new object, the territorial state. Phrases like “the country of Cairo” (bilad misr) were shortened to just misr, and the word came to be used interchangeably for the city and the country. Modern scholars, accustomed to thinking of all history as the history of nationstates, began to write anachronistically of the Ottoman province of “Egypt” (instead of Cairo). The term Egypt had come to refer to a spatial unit identified by geographical boundaries. The older phrases did not picture a territorial object but referred to the place in terms of a relationship—the connection between a city and hinterland.
zh: 民族国家的形成相对晚近，这一点被通常用来翻译19世纪阿拉伯地名的英文词语所掩盖。奥斯曼帝国的省份一般以其统治城市的名称为称呼。
穆罕默德·阿里是 Misr（即开罗）省的总督。这个词所指的不只是城市，而是城市及其乡野，即从政治上和物质上供养它的城镇与村庄腹地。“开罗地区”和“开罗乡野”之类的说法也表达这一含义。

然而，从19世纪后期起，开罗一词（misr）也被引申用来描述一个新客体，即领土国家。“开罗之国”（bilad misr）之类的说法被简化为 misr，这个词开始交替用于城市和国家。习惯于把一切历史都视为民族国家历史的现代学者，开始时代错置地书写奥斯曼帝国的“埃及”省（而非开罗省）。埃及一词已开始指称一个由地理边界确认的空间单位。较早的说法所描绘的不是一个领土客体，而是以关系来指称这个地方——城市与腹地之间的联系。

en: One might suppose that the Lower Nile valley, compared to many other parts of the world, offered a well-defined geography and history within which to imagine a self-contained society. It should have been relatively easy to picture Egypt as a self-sufficient nation, to minimize the wider relations people may have had with other regions, and to give its particular mixture of communities a singular and self-contained past. The survival of monuments from more than five thousand years before, indeed the powerful image of what we call “ancient Egypt” as the cradle of civilization, would seem to offer modern Egyptian nationalism a neat and uncontroversial way to lay together superincumbent images of people, place, and past.
zh: 人们或许会设想，与世界许多其他地区相比，下尼罗河谷提供了明确界定的地理和历史，可以在其中想象一个自足的社会。把埃及描绘成一个自给自足的民族，尽量缩小人们与其他地区可能有的更广泛关系，并给它特定的社群混合体一个单一而自足的过去，本应相对容易。五千多年前的纪念物存留至今，事实上，我们所称的“古埃及”作为文明摇篮的强有力形象，似乎为现代埃及民族主义提供了一种整洁而无争议的方式，把人民、地点和过去的层层叠合意象凑到一起。

en: Yet constructing the past is never so straightforward. In the first place, ancient monuments do not automatically belong to one’s own past. As someone from England, I can admire the imaginative power and ancient precision of Stonehenge, but I cannot feel those stones as part of my own past. In order to belong to one’s history, monuments must connect with some aspect of one’s social identity. Something similar seems to be true of the way the monuments of ancient Egypt figure in the politics of Egyptian nationalism. Periodically an effort was made to present the Pharaonic past as a source of modern Egyptian national identity. The idea that modern Egypt is a society whose ancestry goes back in a continuous line to a Pharaonic beginning is also the view of the nation’s history found in Egyptian school textbooks.
However, such uses of the past have generally been of limited political use in the country’s modern politics.
zh: 然而，建构过去从来不是如此直截了当。首先，古代纪念物不会自动属于某人自己的过去。作为一个来自英格兰的人，我可以赞赏巨石阵的想象力和古代精确性，但我无法感觉那些石头是我自己过去的一部分。纪念物要属于一个人的历史，就必须与这个人社会身份的某个方面发生联系。古埃及纪念物在埃及民族主义政治中的呈现方式，似乎也类似。人们不时努力把法老时代过去呈现为现代埃及民族认同的源泉。认为现代埃及是一个祖先可沿连续谱系上溯至法老开端的社会的观念，也是埃及教科书中对本民族历史的看法。
然而，在国家的现代政治中，这种对过去的利用一般只具有有限的政治用途。

en: The most sustained effort to invoke the glories of ancient Egypt as the source of modern Egyptian identity came in the second quarter of the twentieth century, following the discovery of Tutankhamen’s tomb in the Valley of the Kings, near Luxor, in 1922. When the British archaeologist Howard Carter unearthed the riches of the first royal tomb to be found intact in modern times, the event attracted worldwide attention. The discovery coincided with Egypt’s winning partial independence from the British military occupation established in 1882, and provided the new nationalist government with a powerful expression of the nation’s identity. The government refused to allow the British archaeologists to take possession of 50 percent of the discovered treasure, the practice followed with earlier finds.

Its determination to keep control of the treasure provided a useful demonstration of the government’s newly acquired authority. Yet in the years following this event, the Pharaonic past played only a subordinate and diminishing role in Egyptian nationalism.
zh: 把古埃及的荣耀援引为现代埃及认同源泉的最持久努力，出现在20世纪第二个四分之一时期；此前，1922年在卢克索附近帝王谷发现了图坦卡蒙陵墓。当英国考古学家霍华德·卡特发掘出现代以来第一座完整无损的王陵中的财宝时，这一事件吸引了全世界的注意。这次发现恰逢埃及从1882年建立的英国军事占领下赢得部分独立，为新成立的民族主义政府提供了对民族认同的有力表达。政府拒绝让英国考古学家按以往发现物的惯例占有出土财宝的50%。
它坚持控制这些财宝，有效地展示了政府新获得的权威。然而在此后的岁月里，法老时代的过去在埃及民族主义中只扮演了次要且日渐式微的角色。

en: In architecture, a neo-Pharaonic style came briefly into fashion, but its importance lasted less than a decade.

For a few more years, a group of conservative writers with cultural ties to Europe continued to insist on the significance of the nation’s Pharaonic origins. But they did so as part of an argument against northern Europeans who insisted on the Oriental and therefore backward character of Egypt, and against local intellectuals who insisted on the exclusively Islamic character of their society. The writers’ concern was to show that Egypt was a modern, Western nation, a view to be proven by the fact that the West’s own past lay within Egypt. The significance of the past for these writers was not so much that it gave the nation a distinct and authentic identity, but that it showed that the nation belonged to the larger community of the West, and was therefore modern. The role of the past, in Dirks’s phrase, was to serve as a sign of the modern.
zh: 在建筑领域，新法老风格曾短暂流行，但其重要性持续不到十年。

此后几年间，一群与欧洲有文化联系的保守作家继续坚持本民族法老起源的重要意义。但他们这样做，是作为一场论辩的一部分：既反对坚持埃及的东方性、因而落后性的北欧人，也反对坚持其社会纯粹伊斯兰特性的本地知识分子。这些作家关心的是表明埃及是一个现代的西方国家；他们用西方自己的过去位于埃及这一点来证明这一观点。对这些作家而言，过去的意义与其说在于赋予民族独特而真实的认同，不如说在于表明这个民族属于更大的西方共同体，因而是现代的。用迪尔克斯的话说，过去的作用是充当现代的标志。

en: In the same period a right-wing populist party, Young Egypt (Misr alFatah), began to emphasize the importance of the Pharaonic past, finding there an expression of its belief in leader worship, militarism, and an Egyptian imperialism stretching from the Mediterranean to the equator. This too was short-lived. By the 1930s most political argument in Egypt had reverted to themes that connected more readily with people’s everyday experience and self-conception, principally the themes of Islam, Arabism, and anti-imperialism.
These political identifications did not necessarily refer to the confines of the Nile valley, and gave local politics a much wider resonance than a purely Egyptian nationalism.
zh: 同一时期，右翼民粹政党“青年埃及”（Misr al-Fatah）开始强调法老时代过去的重要性，在其中找到了对其领袖崇拜、军国主义以及从地中海延伸到赤道的埃及帝国主义的信念表达。这也为时短暂。到1930年代，埃及的大部分政治论辩已回到与人们日常经验和自我理解更易相连的主题，主要是伊斯兰、阿拉伯主义和反帝国主义。
这些政治认同未必局限于尼罗河谷，它们赋予地方政治比纯粹埃及民族主义广泛得多的共鸣。

en: The difficulties and ambiguities in the production of the nation’s past can be more fully understood if one shifts one’s attention from the history of nationalism, as it is conventionally written, to the political process that I call making the nation. I find it useful here to think in terms of Bhabha’s distinction between the nation as pedagogy and the nation as performance.

The history of nationalism reconstructs the more or less coherent story of how the nation emerges as a pedagogical object. It pieces together the official nation that is invoked in the ideology of political parties, the propaganda of government programs, the imagery of a national film industry, the rhetoric of school textbooks, the memoirs of public officials, and the news reporting and opinion making of the mass media. These sources constitute the formal archive examined by any standard history of the emergence of twentieth-century Egyptian nationalism.

What such an account generally overlooks is the more mundane and uncertain process of producing the nation. I have in mind the variety of efforts, projects, encounters, and struggles in which the nation and its modern identity are staged and performed. The difference between performance and pedagogy is not a question of looking at the practical realm rather than a realm of ideas, or the local rather than the national. Both pedagogy and performance involve the making of meaning, and both take place in particular sites among particular parties. What is different about making the nation is that it always involves the question of otherness.
zh: 如果人们把注意力从通常书写的民族主义史转向我称之为“造就民族”的政治过程，就能更充分地理解制造民族过去过程中的困难和含混。在此，我觉得用巴巴关于民族作为教育（pedagogy）与民族作为表演（performance）的区分来思考是有用的。
民族主义史重构的，是民族如何作为一个教育客体出现的大致连贯的故事。它拼合出官方民族：政党意识形态、政府计划的宣传、国家电影工业的影像、教科书修辞、公职人员回忆录，以及大众媒体的新闻报道和舆论制造所援引的那个民族。这些来源构成任何标准20世纪埃及民族主义兴起史所考察的正式档案。
这种叙述通常忽视的，是制造民族这一更为平庸和不确定的过程。我想到的是民族及其现代认同在其中被搬演和表演的各种努力、计划、遭遇和斗争。表演与教育的区别，并不是考察实践领域而非观念领域、考察地方而非全国的问题。教育和表演都涉及意义的制造，都发生在特定场所、特定各方之间。造就民族的不同之处在于，它总是涉及他者性问题。

en: In the nation as pedagogy, the emergence of the national community is understood as the history of a self that comes to awareness, or of a people that begins to imagine its peoplehood. History is written to describe the growing self-awareness or imagination of a collective subject. This imagination takes the form of a gradual revealing of the collective subject to itself, a revelation shaped by those powers of communication, reason, and consciousness that define our understanding of an emergent self. There is no encounter with otherness, except as part of the general discovery of a world beyond the self. In the performative making of the nation, on the other hand, otherness plays a constitutive role. The nation is made not out of a process of self-awareness, but out of encounters in which this self is to be made out of others; or rather, is to be made by making-other. The nation is made out of projects in which the identity of the community as a modern nation can be realized only by distinguishing what belongs to the nation from what does not, and by performing this distinction in particular encounters. Unlike conventional accounts of the emergence of the nation as pedagogy, our understanding of such encounters cannot be governed by the consciousness of a collective subject that produces the meaning of the nation; this collective subject, the nation, is not the author of the performance, only its occasional effect. Moreover, one can bring into view the forms of difficulty, uncertainty, violence, and subversion that the production of the nation may involve.
zh: 在作为教育的民族中，民族共同体的出现被理解为自我达到意识的历史，或一个人民开始想象其人民性的历史。历史的书写旨在描述一个集体主体日益增长的自我意识或想象。这种想象采取的形式是集体主体逐渐向自身显现；这一显现由交流、理性和意识的力量所塑造，而这些力量界定了我们对一个生成中自我的理解。除作为对自我之外世界的一般发现的一部分外，这里没有与他者的遭遇。另一方面，在民族的表演性制造中，他者性起着构成性作用。民族不是通过自我意识的过程造就的，而是通过一些遭遇造就的；在这些遭遇中，这个自我要从他者中造出，或者更确切地说，要通过“制造他者”来造就。民族由一些计划造就；在其中，共同体作为现代民族的认同只能通过区分属于民族之物与不属于民族之物、并在特定遭遇中表演这种区分来实现。与关于民族作为教育而出现的常规叙述不同，我们对这类遭遇的理解不能由一个生产民族意义的集体主体的意识来支配；这个集体主体即民族，并不是表演的作者，只是其偶然效果。此外，人们可以看到制造民族可能涉及的各种困难、不确定性、暴力和颠覆。

en: In Egypt, one of the most important figures in this process of making the self through making-other is the figure of the peasant. In the preceding two chapters I examined a variety of mostly foreign representations of the peasant. The new national elite within Egypt developed a more complex relationship to the countryside, a theme that figured prominently in early nationalist fiction, film, and political argument. This chapter takes two interconnected episodes from twentieth-century Egypt, both concerned with the politics of national identity and cultural heritage, and both involving the lives of a local village community. One is a campaign launched in the 1940s to define and preserve a national cultural heritage, pursued through a struggle to create a national architecture based on the vernacular forms of the Egyptian village. The other is a dispute over the protection and presentation of the heritage of ancient Egypt, in particular the Theban Necropolis near Luxor where Howard Carter earlier unearthed the treasures of King Tutankhamen. In 1945 these two different efforts to produce and defend a national heritage came together in the plans to demolish and rebuild a village in southern Egypt. In the 1990s, more than half a century later, the village remained the site of an unresolved struggle over the country’s national heritage.
zh: 在埃及，通过制造他者来制造自我的过程中，最重要的人物之一是农民。在之前两章中，我考察了多种关于农民的再现，其中大多来自国外。埃及国内的新民族精英与乡村发展出更为复杂的关系，这一主题在早期民族主义小说、电影和政治论辩中十分突出。本章选取20世纪埃及两个相互关联的插曲，二者都关涉民族认同与文化遗产的政治，都涉及一个地方村庄共同体的生活。一是1940年代发起的一场界定和保护民族文化传统的运动，其途径是争取创造一种以埃及乡村本土形式为基础的民族建筑。二是关于保护和展示古埃及遗产的争端，尤其是卢克索附近底比斯墓地，霍华德·卡特此前正是在那里发掘出图坦卡蒙王的珍宝。1945年，这两种制造和捍卫民族传统的不同努力，在拆除并重建埃及南部一个村庄的计划中汇合。半个多世纪后的1990年代，这个村庄仍是围绕该国民族传统进行的一场未决斗争的地点。

en: making the nation
zh: 造就民族

en: In 1945 the Antiquities Department of the Egyptian government commissioned the Cairo architect Hassan Fathy to design and build a village to rehouse the inhabitants of the village of Gurna. The village lay on the west bank of the river Nile opposite the town of Luxor, four hundred miles south of Cairo, adjacent to Shahhat’s village of Buʿairat, which we were introduced to in chapter 4. It consisted of a group of hamlets stacked along the desert escarpment at the valley’s edge, amid the ancient rock-cut tombs and funerary temples known as the Theban Necropolis. A year or two earlier the Department of Antiquities had been embarrassed by the removal of an entire wall of one of the ancient tombs under its guard. It blamed the local inhabitants for the theft and decided they should be removed from the hillside and housed in a new village, to be built amid the sugarcane fields of the valley below.
zh: 1945年，埃及政府文物局委托开罗建筑师哈桑·法西设计并建造一座村庄，重新安置古尔纳村的居民。该村位于尼罗河西岸，与卢克索镇隔河相望，在开罗以南四百英里处，毗邻我们在第4章认识的沙哈特所在的布艾拉特村。它由一组小村组成，沿着谷地边缘的沙漠陡坡层叠而建，散布在古代岩凿陵墓和祭祀神庙之间，这一带被称为底比斯墓地。一两年前，文物局管辖的一座古墓整面墙壁被盗走，使其大为难堪。文物局把盗窃归咎于当地居民，决定把他们迁离山坡，安置到谷地甘蔗田中新建的一座村庄里。

en: Hassan Fathy was a visionary architect. In Gurna he pioneered the adoption of what later came to be known as “appropriate technology.” Believing in the value and virtue of vernacular building methods, he rejected the use of reinforced concrete and mass-produced red brick—materials that were already becoming the standard in public housing projects—and insisted on building with handmade bricks produced in the local manner from mud, mixed with straw and dried in the sun. Mud brick was more affordable, he argued, especially if the villagers themselves were allowed to participate in the building, making their own bricks out of local earth, and provided better insulation against the heat of summer. It was also more aesthetically pleasing, he believed, especially when used not just for walls but also for roofs, which could be made to support themselves in the form of elegant vaults and domes. Fathy built New Gurna as a model village to demonstrate the affordability and beauty of this vernacular peasant architecture. He intended it as a prototype, not only for other public housing projects in Egypt, but for the development of an Egyptian national style.
zh: 哈桑·法西是一位有远见的建筑师。在古尔纳，他率先采用后来被称为“适宜技术”的做法。他相信乡土建造方法的价值与优点，拒绝使用钢筋混凝土和批量生产的红砖——这些材料当时正成为公共住房项目的标准——坚持用当地方式手工制作土坯砖：泥土掺入稻草，在阳光下晒干。他认为土坯砖更经济，尤其是如果允许村民自己参与建造、用本地泥土制作砖块，而且对夏季暑热有更好的隔热效果。他还相信，土坯砖在审美上也更悦人，尤其当它不仅用于墙体，也用于屋顶时；屋顶可以以优雅的拱顶和穹顶形式支撑自身。法西把新古尔纳建成模范村，以展示这种乡土农民建筑的经济与美丽。他打算把它作为原型，不仅用于埃及其他公共住房项目，也用于发展一种埃及民族风格。

en: New Gurna became internationally famous. Its construction announced the rejection of modernism in architecture and the desire to reappropriate the styles and materials of an indigenous national heritage. The building of the model village also marked, as Kees van der Spek notes, the moment of this vernacular style’s untimely death.

The government purchased fifty acres of sugarcane land in 1945, a dike was built to keep out the irrigation water, and the construction of the village proceeded over the following three winters. In 1948, with only a fifth of the village completed, Fathy was forced to abandon the project, partly because of bickering between government departments, but mostly because one night that winter men from the old hamlets of Gurna, whose families opposed the planned eviction and resettlement, cut the dike and flooded the low-lying village.
zh: 新古尔纳闻名国际。它的建造宣告了对建筑现代主义的拒绝，以及重新占有本土民族传统的风格与材料的愿望。正如基斯·范德施佩克所指出的，这座模范村的建造也标志着这种乡土风格不合时宜的死亡时刻。
政府于1945年购买了五十费丹甘蔗田，修建堤坝阻挡灌溉水，随后三个冬天里村庄建设持续推进。1948年，村庄只完成五分之一，法西就被迫放弃工程，部分原因是政府部门之间的争吵，但主要是因为那年冬天的一个夜晚，古尔纳旧小村的人——其家族反对计划中的迁离和重新安置——挖开堤坝，淹没了地势低洼的村庄。

en: Fathy’s account of these events, published twenty years later, expresses his disappointment at the failure of his plans “to revive the peasant’s faith in his own culture” and his bitterness toward the “suspicious and strict” inhabitants of Gurna who had refused to cooperate and “were not able to put into words even their material requirements in housing.”

It is easy to criticize Fathy today, whether for his paternalism toward villagers who stood in the way of his architectural vision, or for the cosmopolitanism that led him to propagate this vision in widely admired books published in English and French but cut him off from those who preferred to read in Arabic.

My concern here is not with Hassan Fathy, however, but with those events in the 1940s in Gurna, where the attempt to reappropriate and preserve an Egyptian vernacular was simultaneously born and destroyed. It is this relationship between culture and destruction, between national heritage and its subversion, that I am going to explore. Why did the manufacture of the modern vernacular, the attempt to revive or preserve a peasant culture, as well as the protection of a more ancient, archaeological past, seem to depend upon a relationship of force and a structure of antagonism? Is there something larger one can learn from the fact that the birth of a national heritage movement in New Gurna based upon the building methods of peasant architecture was also the moment of its violent demise?
zh: 法西对这些事件的记述在二十年后出版，表达了他对复兴农民对自己文化之信念的计划失败的失望，以及对古尔纳“多疑而严苛”的居民的怨恨——他们拒绝合作，“甚至无法用语言表达自己对住房的物质需求”。
今天批评法西很容易：或是指责他对阻碍其建筑愿景的村民采取家长式态度，或是指责他的世界主义——这让他在以英文和法文出版、广受赞赏的著作中传播这一愿景，却使他与那些更愿意读阿拉伯文的人相隔绝。

然而，我在这里关心的不是哈桑·法西，而是1940年代古尔纳的那些事件：重新占有并保存一种埃及乡土形式的尝试，同时诞生又同时被摧毁。我要探讨的，正是文化与毁灭之间、民族传统与其颠覆之间的这种关系。为什么现代乡土形式的制造，复兴或保存农民文化的尝试，以及对更古老的考古过去的保护，似乎都依赖于一种武力关系和一种对抗结构？新古尔纳以农民建筑的建造方法为基础的民族传统运动，其诞生同时又是其暴力终结的时刻，我们能否从中领悟某种更广泛的东西？

en: The history of Hassan Fathy’s vernacular model village intersects with a continuing effort to present and preserve a different national heritage, the monuments of ancient Egypt. Fifty years later, toward the close of the twentieth century, the road past New Gurna was filled with tourist buses, which stopped beyond the village at the Colossi of Memnon before proceeding to the Valley of the Kings and other ancient sites. None of the buses ever stopped at the model village, which was barely visible behind the police inspection points and tourist signs that lined the main road.“The Village,” as locals still referred to the place, was a thriving community, but Fathy’s houses were by now overlaid with additions and extra floors (to the extent that domed roofs allowed), or in many cases pulled down. Fathy’s village school, whose domed roof had collapsed from neglect, was demolished by the Ministry of Education in the late 1980s and replaced with a larger school built according to the ministry’s uniform design for all schools, with a reinforced concrete frame and manufactured brick. The handmade mud bricks of the original school were used as rubble to make the new building’s driveway.
zh: 哈桑·法西乡土模范村的历史，与一项持续的努力相交织：展示和保护另一种民族传统，即古埃及的纪念物。五十年后，临近20世纪末，新古尔纳旁的道路挤满了旅游巴士，它们在村外门农巨像处停留，然后前往帝王谷和其他古迹。没有一辆巴士在模范村停留；在主干道两旁警察检查站和旅游标牌的遮挡下，村庄几乎看不见。当地人仍把这里称为“村子”，它是一个兴旺的共同体，但法西的房屋此时已被加建和加盖的楼层覆盖（在穹顶屋顶允许的范围内），或许多已被拆除。法西的村校穹顶因无人照管而坍塌，1980年代后期被教育部拆除，代之以一栋更大的学校，按该部为所有学校设计的统一图纸建造，采用钢筋混凝土框架和机制砖。原校舍的手工土坯砖被当作碎石，铺成新建筑的汽车道。

en: One thing, however, survived intact after more than fifty years: the unfulfilled desire to evict the inhabitants of the old village of Gurna. After several intervening failures, between 1992 and 1994 new plans were drawn up, as part of a master plan for Luxor funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), to depopulate the seven or eight hamlets on the Gurna escarpment, from Sawalim in the north to Gurnat Marʿi in the south, as well as the neighboring hamlet of Medinat Habu (the home of Critchfield’s Shahhat).

Over the following four years new villages again were built, this time located in the desert five to ten kilometers north of old Gurna, and again the households of Gurna largely refused to move and see their village demolished. On January 17, 1998, after several earlier skirmishes, a government bulldozer accompanied by two truckloads of armed police moved into Gurna to carry out demolitions. A group of about three hundred villagers gathered, later swelling to several thousand, and drove the police back with stones, pushing their bulldozer into a canal. The police opened fire on the villagers with automatic rifles, killing four and leaving more than twenty injured.

This incident set back the relocation plans, but by the end of the same year the head of Luxor City Council, Major General Selmi Selim, confirmed that the plans to depopulate “nine shanty areas known as Old Gurna” would go ahead, as part of a vision to turn the area into “an open air museum and cultural preserve.”
As he explained to the press,“You can’t afford to have this heritage wasted because of informal houses being built in an uncivilized manner.”
zh: 然而，有一件事在五十多年后完好无损地留存下来：迁走古尔纳旧村居民这一未实现的愿望。在中间几度失败之后，1992至1994年间又制定了新计划，作为美国国际开发署（USAID）资助的卢克索总体规划的一部分，目的是清空古尔纳陡坡上七到八个小村，从北部的萨瓦利姆到南部的古尔纳特马尔伊，以及邻近的美迪内特哈布小村（克里奇菲尔德笔下沙哈特的家乡）。
此后四年间再次建造了新村庄，这次位于旧古尔纳以北五到十公里的沙漠中，而古尔纳的家庭再次大多拒绝搬迁、拒绝眼看自己的村庄被拆毁。1998年1月17日，在之前数次小冲突之后，一辆政府推土机在两卡车武装警察的护送下开进古尔纳，实施拆除。约三百名村民聚集起来，后来增至数千人，用石头击退警察，把推土机推入一条水渠。警察用自动步枪向村民开枪，打死四人，打伤二十多人。
这一事件使搬迁计划受挫，但同年年底，卢克索市议会主席塞尔米·塞利姆少将确认，清空“被称为旧古尔纳的九个棚户区”的计划将继续进行，这是把该地区变为“露天博物馆和文化保护区”愿景的一部分。
他向媒体解释说：“你不可能承受任由这份遗产因为以不文明方式搭建的非正规房屋而被糟蹋。”

en: The major general’s understanding of “heritage” was very different from Hassan Fathy’s. Fathy had never succeeded in persuading the Egyptian government that it had anything to learn from the peasant. His conviction that a modern, national style, as well as solutions to the practical problems of modernity, could be found in the ways villagers had traditionally done things had no place in official visions of technical development and a tourist-based heritage industry. Yet for all their differences, the two perhaps had something in common. The major general’s use of the term “uncivilized” to justify the evictions echoed the earlier language of Hassan Fathy. Fathy’s account of the events of the 1940s tells the history of planning and building New Gurna as a story of the progress of culture and intelligence, impeded by the ignorance and lawlessness of the natives. The families of Gurna lived mostly as tomb robbers, Fathy said (an accusation to which I will come back), and it was to preserve this lawless way of life that they sabotaged his project. (In the plans for the model village there were to be several public buildings, including a theater and an exhibition hall, intended to create the kind of public spirit that Fathy felt was missing in ordinary villages; but there was also to be another kind of building not usually found in villages, a police station.) This violence and lawlessness provided the pretext for building the new village. It was only by addressing the problems of the ignorance of the peasant and the absence of civilization that an architect interested in a program to create a modern, peasant vernacular could find an opportunity to work. There had to be some lack, something missing from the peasant, for even a sympathetic modernizer to transform his house into a national style.
zh: 这位少将对“遗产”的理解与哈桑·法西大不相同。法西从未成功说服埃及政府：它可以从农民那里学到任何东西。他坚信，一种现代民族风格，以及对现代性实际问题的解决办法，都可以在村民传统的行事方式中找到；这种信念在关于技术发展和旅游遗产产业的官方愿景中没有位置。然而，尽管二者有种种差异，他们或许仍有共同之处。少将用“不文明”一词为驱逐行动辩护，这呼应了哈桑·法西早先的语言。法西对1940年代事件的叙述，把新古尔纳的规划和建造史讲成一个文化与智识进步的故事，而这种进步受到当地人无知和不法的阻碍。法西说，古尔纳的家庭大多以盗墓为生（我稍后会回到这一指控），而他们破坏他的工程，正是为了维持这种不守法的生活方式。（模范村的规划中原本要有若干公共建筑，包括一座剧院和一座展览馆，意在营造法西觉得普通村庄所缺乏的公共精神；但还要有另一种村里通常见不到的建筑——警察局。）这种暴力与不法，为建造新村提供了借口。只有着手解决农民无知和文明缺失的问题，一位有志于创造现代农民乡土风格的建筑师才能找到工作的机会。农民身上必须有所匮乏、有所缺失，即便是富有同情心的现代化者，才能把他的房屋转化为民族风格。

en: I want to begin my analysis of Fathy’s project by recalling what seems a minor episode in his account, an event he refers to as the malaria epidemic of 1947. He notes in passing that the epidemic “killed about a third of Gurna’s inhabitants,” but concentrates more on the restrictions imposed on travel from Cairo and other delays the epidemic caused to his project.

It seems startling today that Fathy would not discuss any larger objections to uprooting a community in the midst of such suffering. But in fact there is more to this oversight. Writing twenty years later, Fathy had collapsed together two epidemics. And these events were not just an obstacle to his plans, but the source of the political circumstances that made them possible.
zh: 我想从法西叙述中一个看似次要的插曲开始分析他的工程，即他所说的1947年疟疾流行病。他顺便提到，这场流行病“杀死了古尔纳约三分之一的居民”，但更多关注的是流行病导致的开罗往来限制，以及对他工程造成的其他延误。
法西没有讨论在如此苦难之中连根拔起一个共同体是否会遭到更大反对，这在今天看来令人吃惊。但实际上，这一疏忽还有更深的内容。法西在二十年后写作时，把两场流行病混为一谈。而这些事件不只是他计划的障碍，也是使计划得以可能的政治环境的来源。

en: The 1947 epidemic was actually an outbreak of cholera, not malaria, and affected mostly Lower Egypt, although restrictions were placed on travel to and from the south (Fathy helped the villagers in Gurna to sterilize their wells as a measure against any local outbreak). But a few years earlier, in 1942–45, an epidemic of malaria had occurred in the Luxor region, the outbreak of gambiae malaria, the disease’s most lethal form, that I discussed in chapter 1. Brought from the south by recent irrigation work designed to increase the sugarcane plantations, as I mentioned, and by increased wartime traffic with Sudan, it was this earlier epidemic, along with the famine that resulted from wartime food shortages and men too sick to harvest the wheat crop or earn wages cutting cane, that killed more than a third of the people in the Gurna region.

Among the 100,000 to 200,000 people who died in the south, the heaviest casualties were in Gurna and other sugarcane plantations, where perennial irrigation enabled the gambiae mosquito to reproduce. It was the manager of the plantation neighboring the Gurna sugar estate who estimated in May 1944 that 80 to 90 percent of the local population had contracted the disease, and the doctor in the nearest town on the west bank, Armant, who reported 80 to 90 deaths a day.
Hassan Fathy arrived in Gurna only a few months after the last gambiae mosquito was killed, before the survivors in the local villages had even gathered another harvest.
zh: 1947年的流行病实际上是霍乱，不是疟疾，主要影响下埃及，尽管当时对南方的往来实施了限制（法西帮助古尔纳村民对水井消毒，以防当地爆发疫情）。但几年前，即1942—1945年，卢克索地区曾发生一场疟疾流行病，即我在第1章讨论过的冈比亚疟疾，这是该疾病最致命的形式。正如我提到的，它由南方输入，源于为扩大甘蔗种植园而新近进行的灌溉工程，以及战时与苏丹往来的增加；正是这场较早的流行病，加上战时粮食短缺和男子因病重而无法收割小麦或挣取砍甘蔗工资所造成的饥荒，夺去了古尔纳地区三分之一以上的人的生命。
在南方死亡的10万至20万人中，伤亡最重的是古尔纳和其他甘蔗种植园，那里的常年灌溉使冈比亚蚊得以繁殖。1944年5月，古尔纳糖业庄园邻接种植园的经理估计，当地人口的80%至90%已感染该病；西岸最近城镇阿曼特的医生则报告每天有80至90人死亡。
哈桑·法西抵达古尔纳时，最后一只冈比亚蚊刚刚被消灭几个月，当地村庄的幸存者甚至还没有收获下一季作物。

en: The gambiae malaria epidemic, as we saw in chapter 1, provoked a political crisis in Cairo. Opposition politicians blamed the large number of deaths on the poverty of the Luxor region and the rest of the extreme south, where a handful of owners controlled most of the land in sugar plantations of thousands of acres each, and the majority of the population was landless and worked for starvation wages. A deputy in parliament argued that living conditions in the Soviet Union were far better. The ruling Wafd party, which expressed the interests of large landowners, was anxious to defuse this radical threat to the principle of landownership. It argued that the cause of the epidemic was not poverty and inequality but the unsanitary living conditions in the villages. Instead of land reform and the redistribution of wealth, it supported a plan to demolish the country’s villages and replace them with well-ventilated, sanitary, and attractive model villages.
zh: 正如我们在第1章所看到的，冈比亚疟疾流行病在开罗引发了政治危机。反对派政治家把大量死亡归咎于卢克索地区和整个极南地区的贫困：那里少数所有者控制着大部分土地，每个甘蔗种植园动辄数千费丹，而大多数人口无地，靠饥饿工资劳作。一名议会代表争辩说，苏联的生活条件要好得多。执政的华夫脱党代表大地主的利益，急于化解这一对土地所有权原则的激进威胁。它主张，流行病的起因不是贫困和不平等，而是村庄不卫生的生活条件。它不支持土地改革和财富再分配，而是支持一项计划：拆除全国村庄，代之以通风良好、卫生且美观的模范村。

en: The idea of solving the problems of the countryside by replacing village housing with model villages had been promoted by a new generation of sociologists, educators, medical experts, and architects.

In 1933 the Royal Agricultural Society built a model ʿizba (housing complex) on its estate at Bahtim, near Cairo, and in 1940 gave Hassan Fathy his first large architectural commission, to build a second ʿizba at the same site.

Henry Ayrout, whose father and brothers were architects practicing in Cairo, promoted the rebuilding of the country’s villages in his study of the Egyptian peasant, Moeurs et coutumes des fellahs (Paris, 1938), which was republished in Cairo in French and Arabic editions in 1942 and English in 1945.
In 1941 the Cairo architectural review al-ʿImara launched a campaign for village reconstruction and published a plan for a model village.
None of these proposals received government funding, until the political crisis of 1944–45, when Hassan Fathy was invited by the Antiquities Department to construct his model village at Gurna.
zh: 用模范村取代村庄住房以解决乡村问题的想法，受到新一代社会学家、教育家、医学专家和建筑师的推动。
1933年，皇家农业协会在开罗附近的巴赫提姆庄园建造了一座模范伊兹巴（住宅建筑群），并于1940年交给哈桑·法西第一项大型建筑委托，在同一地点建造第二座伊兹巴。
亨利·艾鲁特的父亲和兄弟都是在开罗执业的建筑师，他在其埃及农民研究《费拉欣的风俗与习惯》（巴黎，1938）中提倡重建全国村庄；该书于1942年以法文和阿拉伯文版在开罗再版，1945年又出英文版。
1941年，开罗建筑评论杂志《建筑》（al-ʿImara）发起了一场村庄重建运动，并公布了一份模范村规划。
这些提议都没有得到政府资助，直到1944—1945年的政治危机，哈桑·法西才应文物局之邀，在古尔纳建造他的模范村。

en: The government purchased the fifty acres of sugarcane land from Boulos Hanna Pasha, who owned thousands of acres in the Gurna region and was one of the largest landowners in Upper Egypt. The fifty acres were to provide space for the village with its generously proportioned houses and its numerous public buildings, a freshwater pond for swimming (to keep children from the canals, where they contracted schistosomiasis), and a public park for recreation—but not a single acre on which to grow food. Unable to consider the dangerous question of villagers’ rights to agricultural land, Fathy helped establish a textile workshop, employing twenty child weavers, to provide some income for the village. A visiting government official noticed that the children in the workshop “looked thin and hungry,” and suggested that they be given a bowl of lentil soup every day. “It was a sensible and practical suggestion,” Fathy admits. But no money could be found to provide the food.

The solutions Fathy pursued were architectural and did not address questions of landownership. This was not seen, however, as a limitation. Fathy saw his village as a pilot project launching a “National Program for Rural Reconstruction” that would lead “to the complete regeneration of the Egyptian countryside through rebuilding its villages.”
zh: 政府从布特罗斯·汉纳帕夏手中购买这五十费丹甘蔗田；他在古尔纳地区拥有数千费丹土地，是上埃及最大的土地所有者之一。这五十费丹本要为村庄提供空间——宽敞的房屋、众多公共建筑、一个供游泳的淡水池塘（使儿童不到水渠里去，那里容易感染血吸虫病）和一个供休闲的公园——却没有一费丹用来种植粮食。由于无法考虑村民对农业土地的权利这一危险问题，法西帮助建立了一家纺织作坊，雇用二十名童工织工，为村庄提供一些收入。一位前来视察的政府官员注意到，作坊里的孩子“看起来瘦弱饥饿”，建议每天给他们一碗扁豆汤。“这是一个明智而实际的建议，”法西承认。但找不到钱提供食物。
法西寻求的是建筑上的解决办法，并未触及土地所有权问题。然而，这并未被视为一种局限。法西把自己的村庄看作一个试点项目，启动一项“全国乡村重建计划”，该计划将“通过重建村庄，实现埃及乡村的全面复兴”。

en: This approach to social problems was founded on the belief that the recovery of a vernacular national heritage—a heritage that was pure and undebased, and thus clean and sanitary—would provide a means to the recovery of social energy, health, and purpose. Such thinking went beyond the architectural politics of the later nineteenth century, expressed in the rebuilding of Cairo and other large towns and the construction of workers’ housing on agricultural estates as rectilinear, visually organized spaces.

Planning and rebuilding would now lead to the construction of new peasant selves. At the same time it offered an alternative to impractical and controversial proposals that threatened the social order of landownership. Fathy was a farsighted individual, devoted to the new possibilities of planning and architecture, not just for their end results, but as a process. He insisted on the participation of villagers in the design—a novel idea—and believed the very process of planning would be the means for them to recover their lost individuality (about which Ayrout had written), through developing their power to make decisions. They would develop into subjects of the nation by discovering, in the rebuilding of their heritage, the ability to think for themselves.“Ideally,” Fathy wrote,“if the village were to take three years to build, the designing should go on for two years and eleven months.”
zh: 这种解决社会问题的方法基于一个信念：恢复一种本土民族传统——一种纯洁未损、因而洁净卫生的传统——将提供恢复社会活力、健康和目标的途径。这种思想超越了19世纪后期的建筑政治；后者的表现是重建开罗和其他大城镇，以及在农业庄园上建造作为直线式、视觉化组织空间的工人住房。

现在，规划和重建将导致新农民自我的建构。与此同时，它为一些不切实际、有争议且威胁土地所有权社会秩序的提议提供了替代方案。法西是一位有远见的人，致力于规划和建筑的新可能性——不仅看重其最终结果，也看重其过程。他坚持村民参与设计——这是一个新颖的想法——并相信规划过程本身将成为他们恢复失去的个性（艾鲁特曾写到这一点）的手段，途径是发展他们的决策能力。他们将通过在自己传统的重建中发现独立思考的能力，发展为民族的国民。“理想情况下，”法西写道，“如果村庄需要三年建成，设计就应该持续两年十一个月。”

en: This was a radical view of the possibilities for peasant initiative and peasant culture. The limitation we can now see—the inability to consider that villagers might prefer to stay in the houses they had already designed and built themselves—reflected the new hubris of planning. Fathy prided himself on the fact that in New Gurna, a village intended to house seven thousand people, every house was to be individually designed. Yet this desire embodied a contradiction, the oxymoron of planned individuality. What was distinctive in village housing was precisely that villages never planned their houses as finished objects. They built them to grow with the households and activities they housed, expanding and subdividing them, adding and removing extra floors, turning rooms into workshops, stables, or storefronts, over years or generations. The irregular streets and interlocking houses that Fathy designed for New Gurna expressed his attempt to recreate the way the villagers’ “customs and taboos, their friendships and their disputes [were] intimately integrated into the topography, into every wall and beam of the village.”

But to produce this irregularity as something planned in advance, the houses had to be placed tightly together, so that streets could twist and interlocking relationships find expression in the village’s topography. As a result, the planning provided no space for the houses to be later expanded or reorganized.
zh: 这是关于农民主动性和农民文化可能性的一种激进观点。我们现在能看到的局限——无法考虑村民可能更愿意留在自己已经设计和建造的房屋里——反映了规划的新傲慢。法西引以为豪的是，在新古尔纳这个打算容纳七千人的村庄里，每栋房屋都单独设计。然而这一愿望包含一种矛盾，即“计划性个体性”的悖论。村庄住房的独特之处恰恰在于，村庄从不把房屋规划为完成品。他们建造房屋，使其随所容纳的家庭和活动一起生长：扩展和细分，增加和拆除额外楼层，把房间变成作坊、马厩或店面，历经数年或数代。法西为新古尔纳设计的不规则街道和相互咬合的房子，表达了他试图重现村民的“习俗与禁忌、友谊与纠纷[如何]紧密融入地形，融入村庄每一堵墙、每一根梁”的努力。
但要把这种不规则性作为预先规划的东西生产出来，房屋就必须紧密排列，使街道能够蜿蜒，使相互咬合的关系能够在村庄地形中得到表达。结果，规划没有为房屋日后扩展或重组留出空间。

en: Fathy’s attitudes toward problems of peasant initiative also expressed the fact that he himself was from the landowning class (his father was the owner of one or more estates) and indeed was something of a royalist, with admirers and supporters among the Egyptian royal family, including the sisters of King Farouk.

His architectural commissions came from the same milieu, for only large institutions or wealthy individuals could afford the luxury of architecture. Before receiving the commission to build the village of New Gurna, he designed the model farm for the Royal Agricultural Society (1941) and a headquarters at the Red Sea port of Safaga for the Anglo-American-controlled Chilean Nitrate Company (1942), two institutions supporting large-scale farming. Most of his other architectural designs in this period were country houses for the proprietors of large agricultural estates.
zh: 法西对农民主动性问题的态度，也表明他本人出身于地主阶级（他的父亲拥有一座或数座庄园），事实上还颇有点保王派，在埃及王室中有仰慕者和支持者，包括法鲁克国王的姐妹们。
他的建筑委托来自同一圈子，因为只有大型机构或富人才负担得起建筑这种奢侈品。在接到建造新古尔纳村的委托之前，他为皇家农业协会设计了模范农场（1941），并为英美控制的智利硝石公司在红海港口萨法加设计了总部（1942）；这两个机构都支持大规模农业。这一时期他的其他建筑设计大多是大型农业庄园主人的乡间宅邸。

en: If Fathy saw the villagers of Gurna as unable “to put into words even their material requirements in housing,” when one puts his project into a larger social context it is the architect who is perhaps not able to put into words its material basis. The sugar plantations of the Gurna region had originally been village land. As we saw in chapter 2, from the mid-nineteenth century the ruling household in Cairo began to take over village land, paying little or no compensation, as new irrigation schemes made it possible to channel the annual Nile flood and plant the sugarcane crop year-round. After the country’s Ottoman Turkish ruling household was declared bankrupt by its British and French bankers in 1875 and the British army invaded and occupied Egypt, the foreign bankers managed the estates and then auctioned them off, not returning them to the original village owners but selling them to barons like Boulos Hanna and Ahmad ʿAbbud. In 1908, when the bankers auctioned the former viceregal estates near Gurna, local villagers discovered that their land and even their houses were to become the property of the new plantation owners. When the bailiffs later came to evict the villagers, in one reported instance, they met resistance. Fifteen members of the eviction force were injured, and fifty-seven villagers were arrested, one of who died in custody.

So when the government neglected to provide New Gurna with land to grow its own food, or even bowls of lentil soup for child workers, this was not an insignificant oversight. It was the continuation of a process of expropriation constructed and reconstructed over the preceding hundred years through the depredations of a ruling elite and their European bankers. And it was to counter the new challenges to this coercive order, following the malaria epidemic of 1942–45, that men were dreaming up plans for model villages and Fathy was proclaiming the architect’s unique ability “to revive the peasant’s faith in his own culture.”
zh: 如果说法西认为古尔纳村民无法“甚至用语言表达自己对住房的物质需求”，那么把他的工程放进更大的社会背景中看，或许倒是建筑师无法用语言表达其物质基础。古尔纳地区的甘蔗种植园原本是村庄的土地。正如我们在第2章所见，从19世纪中叶起，开罗的统治家族开始接管村庄土地，几乎不付或完全不付补偿，因为新的灌溉工程使得可以引尼罗河年度泛滥之水，全年种植甘蔗。1875年，该国奥斯曼土耳其统治家族被其英国和法国银行家宣告破产，英国军队入侵并占领埃及；此后外国银行家管理这些庄园，随后将其拍卖，不是归还原来的村庄所有者，而是卖给布特罗斯·汉纳和艾哈迈德·阿布德之类的男爵。1908年，银行家拍卖古尔纳附近的前总督庄园时，当地村民发现自己的土地甚至房屋将成为新种植园主的财产。后来法警前来驱逐村民时，据一则报道，他们遇到了抵抗。驱逐队十五名成员受伤，五十七名村民被捕，其中一人死于羁押。
因此，当政府未能给新古尔纳提供种植粮食的土地，甚至未能为童工提供一碗扁豆汤时，这并非无关紧要的疏忽。这是此前一百年间通过统治精英及其欧洲银行家的掠夺而建构和重建的剥夺过程的延续。而正是在1942—1945年疟疾流行病之后，为了应对对这一强制秩序的新挑战，人们才构想出模范村的计划，法西才宣称建筑师具有“复兴农民对自己文化之信念”的独特能力。

en: In projects of this sort one sees the difficulties of making the nation. To perform the nation, groups must be included by first declaring them excluded for their lack of civilization, villages destroyed in order to preserve them, pasts declared lost so that they may be recovered. Fathy wanted to “revive” an indigenous culture as a means of developing an Egyptian national heritage. To perform this revival, he needed the people of Gurna. Yet he needed them as a people outside the nation, whose removal would help bring the nation and its past into being. The Gurnawis were to be treated as ignorant, uncivilized, and incapable of preserving their own architectural heritage. Only by seeing them in this way would the architect have an opportunity to intervene, presenting himself as the rediscoverer of a local heritage that the locals themselves no longer recognized or knew how to value. As the spokesman bringing this heritage into national politics, the architect would enable the past to speak and play its role in giving the modern nation its character.
zh: 在此类项目中，人们可以看到造就民族的困难。要表演民族，就必须先以缺乏文明为由把某些群体宣布为被排除者，从而将他们纳入；为了保存村庄而将其摧毁，宣布过去已经失落以便将其恢复。法西想“复兴”一种本土文化，作为发展埃及民族传统的手段。要表演这场复兴，他需要古尔纳的人民。然而，他需要他们作为民族之外的人民，他们的迁离将有助于使民族及其过去得以形成。古尔纳人要被当作无知、不文明、无力保护自己建筑遗产的人。只有以这种方式看待他们，建筑师才有机会介入，把自己呈现为当地人自己已不再承认或不懂得珍视的地方传统的重新发现者。作为把这一传统带入民族政治的代言人，建筑师将使过去得以言说，并在赋予现代民族以特性方面发挥作用。

en: The people of Gurna could enter into national politics only by submitting to an act of violence. To preserve their heritage, the architect first had to destroy it. Old Gurna was to be pulled down and rebuilt—and not just because it was built over antiquities, for if the project succeeded, Fathy hoped that every other village of Egypt would also be demolished and rebuilt (a proposal later taken up by the United States development program in Egypt).

The preservation of the past required its destruction so that the past could be rebuilt. Likewise, the performing of the nation required that every one of its rural inhabitants be declared outside the nation, uncivilized and unhygienic, so that in rendering them civilized and clean, the nation could be made.
zh: 古尔纳的人民只有服从一次暴力行为，才能进入民族政治。为了保护他们的传统，建筑师首先必须摧毁它。旧古尔纳将被拆除重建——而且不仅因为它建在古代遗物之上；如果工程成功，法西希望埃及其他每个村庄也都会被拆除重建（这一提议后来被美国在埃及的发展计划采纳）。
保存过去要求摧毁过去，以便过去可以被重建。同样，表演民族要求把每一个乡村居民都宣布为民族之外的人、不文明且不卫生的人，以便在使他们变得文明和洁净的过程中，民族得以造就。

en: When Fathy first visited one of his family’s own large farms, near Talkha in the Nile Delta, “it was a terrible experience,” he reports. “I had had no idea until then of the horrible squalor and ugliness amid which the peasants on a farm lived. I saw a collection of mud huts, low, dark, and dirty, with no windows, no latrines, no clean water, cattle living practically in the same room with people; there was not the remotest connection with the idyllic countryside of my imagination.”

Fathy persuaded his parents to rebuild the workers’ housing, or ʿizba. As he embarked on this and subsequent projects, however, he discovered two difficulties, one aesthetic and one practical. It was the solution to this dual difficulty that was to define the style of building for which he became famous. The genealogy of the solution is important, because it involves a series of interlocking elements over which Fathy had no control. These illuminate the complexities of turning to the peasant, or to the ideal countryside of the imagination, in the attempt to solve national problems and define a national style.
zh: 法西第一次造访自家位于尼罗河三角洲塔勒哈附近的一座大农场时，“那是一次可怕的经历，”他写道。“此前我完全不知道农场上的农民生活在多么可怕的污秽和丑陋之中。我看到一片土屋，低矮、黑暗、肮脏，没有窗户，没有厕所，没有干净的水，牲口几乎和人住在同一间屋里；这与我心目中田园诗般的乡野毫无相似之处。”
法西说服父母重建工人住房，即伊兹巴。然而，当他着手这项工程及随后的项目时，发现了两个困难，一个在审美上，一个在实践上。正是对双重困难的解决办法，界定了后来使他成名的建筑风格。这一解决办法的谱系很重要，因为它涉及一系列法西无法控制的相互关联因素。这些因素揭示了在试图解决民族问题、界定民族风格时转向农民或想象中理想乡野的复杂性。

en: The aesthetic problem was that Fathy was unable to discover a model for the vernacular form he sought to revive in any of the villages he was rebuilding, or any other village he visited in Egypt. The idyllic countryside of his imagination existed nowhere. The practical difficulty was that Egypt was without forests and had no commercial supplies of lumber, which Fathy needed to build the roofs of his mud-brick structures. In 1941, when building the model farm for the Royal Agricultural Society at Bahtim, the difficulty became acute, because the project included large granaries whose roofs spanned a greater width than those of the ordinary workers’ housing. To solve the problem Fathy attempted to build the granary roofs without lumber in the form of vaults and domes, employing the same mud bricks used for the walls. The vaults were intended to support themselves using the principle of the arch, and in turn carry the weight of the domes. This complex method was unsuccessful, however, and the domes collapsed.
zh: 审美问题在于，法西在他所重建的任何村庄，或他在埃及访问过的任何其他村庄，都未能找到自己想要复兴的乡土形式的范本。他想象中的田园乡野在任何地方都不存在。实践上的困难是，埃及没有森林，也没有商业木材供应，而法西需要用木材为土坯建筑建造屋顶。1941年在巴赫提姆为皇家农业协会建造模范农场时，这一困难变得尖锐，因为工程包括大型粮仓，其屋顶跨度比普通工人住房更宽。为解决这一问题，法西尝试不用木材，以拱顶和穹顶的形式建造粮仓屋顶，使用与墙体相同的土坯砖。拱顶意在利用拱的原理支撑自身，进而承载穹顶的重量。然而，这种复杂的方法没有成功，穹顶坍塌了。

en: Hassan Fathy’s brother, ʿAli, who worked as an engineer on the Aswan Dam, helped him overcome the problem. He invited him to come and visit the village of Gharb Aswan, near the dam, where Fathy finally found houses whose roofs included large mud-brick vaults. Gharb Aswan, he wrote,
zh: 哈桑·法西的兄弟阿里是阿斯旺大坝的工程师，帮助他解决了这个问题。他邀请法西去参观大坝附近的西阿斯旺村，法西在那里终于找到了屋顶包含大型土坯拱顶的房屋。他写道，西阿斯旺

en: was a new world for me, a whole village of spacious, lovely, clean, and harmonious houses each more beautiful than the next. There was nothing else like it in Egypt; a village from some dream country . . . whose architecture had been preserved for centuries uncontaminated by foreign influences. . . . Not a trace of the miserly huddle of the usual Egyptian village, but house after house, tall, easy, roofed cleanly with a brick vault. . . . I realized that I was looking at the living survivor of traditional Egyptian architecture.
zh: 对我来说是一个新世界，整个村庄都是宽敞、可爱、洁净而和谐的房子，一栋比一栋美。埃及没有别的地方像它；一个来自某个梦想之国的村庄……它的建筑数百年来保存下来，未受外来影响污染……没有通常埃及村庄那种吝啬拥挤的痕迹，只有一栋接一栋高大的房屋，舒展自如，屋顶由砖拱整洁地覆盖……我意识到，我看到的是传统埃及建筑活着的幸存者。

en: Fathy recruited a master mason from the village, ʿAlaa al-Din Mustafa, who showed him the method of building vaults and worked with him on New Gurna and several of his subsequent projects. The mud-brick vault and dome henceforth defined Fathy’s Egyptian vernacular. At the same time, he believed, by eliminating the use of expensive timber, these methods provided a means of building “an architecture for the poor.”
zh: 法西从该村招募了一位石匠师傅阿拉丁·穆斯塔法，后者向他展示了建造拱顶的方法，并与他一起参与新古尔纳及随后几个项目。土坯拱顶和穹顶从此界定了法西的埃及乡土风格。同时，他相信，通过消除对昂贵木材的使用，这些方法提供了建造“为穷人的建筑”的途径。

en: There were problems with Fathy’s solutions on both counts, the aesthetic and the practical. On the aesthetic side, Gharb Aswan was a Nubian village, and its houses were built in the distinctive style of the Kanuzi, one of the two main Nubian linguistic and cultural groups. Fathy chose to see this style as the survival of a pure Egyptian architecture, “uncontaminated by foreign influences.” The Egyptian government did not recognize the Nubians, whose country spanned the modern border between Egypt and Sudan, as a distinct people or ethnicity, so Fathy’s view of Nubian cultures as Egyptian was in accord with official opinion, even if the Kanuzi themselves might not have considered their heritage Egyptian. Still, it was ironic—and instructive—that only among a people whose language, culture, and history were all different from those said to define modern Egypt could Fathy find an Egypt uncontaminated by the foreign.
The point is not to discredit Fathy’s desire for a vernacular Egyptian architecture, but to acknowledge its complex and heterogenous origins.
zh: 法西的解决办法在审美和实践两方面都有问题。在审美方面，西阿斯旺是一个努比亚村庄，其房屋以卡努齐人独特的风格建造；卡努齐人是努比亚两大语言文化群体之一。法西选择把这种风格视为一种纯粹埃及建筑——“未受外来影响污染”——的存留。埃及政府不承认疆域横跨埃及和苏丹现代边界的努比亚人是一个独特的民族或族群，因此法西把努比亚文化视为埃及文化的观点与官方意见一致，即便卡努齐人自己可能并不认为自己的传统是埃及的。尽管如此，具有讽刺意味——也富有教益——的是，法西只能在一个语言、文化和历史都不同于那些据称界定现代埃及的群体中，找到未被外来因素污染的埃及。
重点不是要否定法西对一种埃及乡土建筑的愿望，而是要承认其复杂而混杂的起源。

en: More of an obstacle to the success of this new aesthetic was that in both Egypt and Nubia domes carried a rather different connotation in vernacular architecture than the meaning Fathy wanted to give them. They were traditionally used only for the roofs of mosques, churches, and tombs. While this association may not have been especially resonant for a cosmopolitan Cairo architect trained in the modernist style, in rural Egypt, especially in the south, domes were used everywhere for the small roofs of saints’ tombs, and never for the building of houses. Despite what many agreed was the powerful simplicity and beauty of Fathy’s designs, he could never erase the existing significance of domes in the countryside, which transformed his own designs into an inappropriate confusion of sacred and domestic styles.
zh: 对这种新审美风格能否成功而言，更大的障碍在于，在埃及和努比亚，穹顶在乡土建筑中承载的含义都与法西想赋予它们的意义相当不同。传统上，穹顶只用于清真寺、教堂和陵墓的屋顶。对于一位受过现代主义风格训练、四海为家的开罗建筑师来说，这种联想或许并不特别强烈；但在埃及乡村，尤其是南部，穹顶到处用于圣徒陵墓的小屋顶，从不用于建造房屋。尽管许多人一致认为法西的设计具有强烈的简洁与美感，他却永远无法抹去穹顶在乡村既有的意义；这一意义使他的设计变成圣俗风格的不当混糅。

en: On the practical side, vaults and domes were a solution to a problem that for most villagers in Egypt did not exist. Fathy found timber expensive— and calculated elaborate mud-brick roofs to be more affordable—because he was obliged to purchase it commercially. For the farm at Bahtim he was building an entire model hamlet, and in particular the large granaries to store the landowner’s grain, something ordinary villagers never had the luxury of needing, so he required timber in large amounts. Egypt imported its commercial timber from Romania. The Second World War cut off these supplies and caused the British army to requisition materials already in the country. The resulting timber shortage obliged Fathy to turn to the more complicated alternative of vaults, which required large quantities of mud brick and the labor of skilled masons.
zh: 在实践方面，拱顶和穹顶所解决的，是埃及大多数村民并不存在的问题。法西觉得木材昂贵——并认为精巧的土坯屋顶更经济——因为他必须从商业渠道购买木材。巴赫提姆的农场是一个完整的模范小村，尤其是那些用来储存地主粮食的大型粮仓，普通村民从未奢侈到需要这样的东西，因此他需要大量木材。埃及的商业木材从罗马尼亚进口。第二次世界大战切断了这些供应，并使英国军队征用该国已有的材料。由此造成的木材短缺迫使法西转向更复杂的拱顶方案，而这需要大量土坯砖和熟练石匠的劳动。

en: In Gurna and other parts of Upper Egypt there was a local method of vaulting using a technique known as tuuf, which was simpler and less expensive than Fathy’s method.

But this was used only in exceptional circumstances, such as where termites were present, and Fathy seems not to have learned of its existence. In most cases villagers made flat roofs from the trunks of locally grown date palms, overlaid with palm stalks and mud plaster. Unlike Fathy, they had no need to purchase commercial supplies of wood. They built their houses themselves, and when it was time to build or extend a house another palm tree could always be found, usually one of the villager’s own. Palms, as it happens, are male or female, and only the latter produce fruit. Just one male tree was needed to fertilize every fifteen or twenty females, so the other males could be cut for timber.
Thanks to the reproductive mechanisms of the date palm, for the villager, unlike the architect, there was no timber shortage, and thus no need for the complexities of domes.
zh: 在古尔纳和上埃及其他地区，有一种使用称作 tuuf 的技术建造拱顶的本地方法，比法西的方法更简单、更便宜。
但它只在特殊情况下使用，例如有白蚁的地方，而法西似乎不知道它的存在。大多数情况下，村民用本地生长的枣椰树干建造平屋顶，上面铺椰枣叶柄和泥灰。与法西不同，他们无需购买商业木材。他们自己建造房屋；到了建造或扩建房屋的时候，总能找到另一棵棕榈树，通常是村民自己的树。棕榈树恰好分雌雄，只有雌树结果。每十五到二十棵雌树只需一棵雄树授粉，因此其余的雄树可以砍作木材。
多亏枣椰树的繁殖机制，对村民来说——与建筑师不同——不存在木材短缺，因此也不需要复杂的穹顶。

en: For reasons both aesthetic and practical, Fathy’s mud-brick domes and vaults never caught on, except among a small group of his students and friends. The use of mud brick for any kind of architecture, moreover, was never supported by Egyptian officialdom or the architectural profession, and large building contractors like Osman Ahmed Osman lobbied successfully against Fathy’s ideas. Villagers continued to build their own houses with mud brick walls. But even these gradually gave way to the use of baked red brick and concrete. Curiously, the elements that were bringing about the demise of this local heritage were the same developments that had enabled Fathy to discover his distinctive style—large-scale agriculture, and the Aswan Dam.
zh: 由于审美和实践两方面的原因，法西的土坯穹顶和拱顶从未流行起来，只在他的一小群学生和朋友中流传。此外，任何建筑使用土坯砖都从未得到埃及官方或建筑界的支持，而奥斯曼·艾哈迈德·奥斯曼之类大型建筑承包商成功游说反对法西的理念。村民继续用土坯砖墙建造自己的房屋。但即便是这些房屋也逐渐让位于烧结红砖和混凝土。奇怪的是，导致这一地方传统消亡的因素，正是使法西得以发现其独特风格的那些发展——大规模农业和阿斯旺大坝。

en: By the end of the 1960s, two decades after the building of New Gurna, the government had taken the place of large landowners in deciding what to grow and had constructed a second dam at Aswan. The High Dam ended the annual flooding of the Nile and enabled the authorities to extend the cultivation of sugarcane, which displaced the growing of wheat. Villagers no longer had the long weeks of the Nile flood, which in the past provided time for the laborious work of brick making and communal house building. Many no longer had their own wheat to provide the straw needed for bricks and plaster. For both these reasons, building with mud brick began to lose its advantages over the faster method of building with reinforced concrete.
zh: 到1960年代末，即新古尔纳建成二十年后，政府已取代大地主来决定种植什么，并在阿斯旺修建了第二座大坝。高坝终结了尼罗河的年度泛滥，使当局得以扩大甘蔗种植，取代了小麦种植。村民不再有尼罗河泛滥时长长的数周时间——过去正是这段时间提供了制作砖块和集体建屋的辛劳工作所需的时间。许多人也不再拥有自己的小麦来提供制砖和抹灰所需的稻草。由于这两个原因，土坯砖建筑开始失去相对于更快速的钢筋混凝土建筑方法的优势。

en: Thanks to the dam, moreover, even the mud itself was less and less available. The fields were no longer flooded, there was no longer an annual deposit of Nile silt, and no longer any renewal of the alluvial mud out of which mud-brick houses were built. Before the High Dam, the Nile carried some 124 million tons of sediment to the sea each year, depositing nearly ten million tons on the flood plain. After the dam, 98 percent of that sediment remained behind the dam.

By the 1980s the government was forced to ban the use of alluvial mud for brick making, to protect agricultural land. Fathy’s celebration of a vernacular based on centuries of accumulation of local mud was launched at precisely the moment when (and for reasons connected with the fact that) the mud for the first time in history was no longer in supply.
zh: 此外，由于大坝，连泥土本身也越来越难以获得。田地不再被水淹，不再有尼罗河淤泥的年度沉积，也不再有用以建造土坯房屋的冲积泥的更新。在高坝之前，尼罗河每年携约1.24亿吨泥沙入海，在洪泛平原上沉积近一千万吨。大坝建成后，这些泥沙的98%滞留在坝后。
到1980年代，政府被迫禁止用冲积泥制砖，以保护农业用地。法西对一种基于数百年本地泥土积累的乡土形式的颂扬，恰好发起于这样一个时刻：历史上第一次，泥土不再有供应（而且其原因正与此相关）。

en: If the irrigation works at Aswan caused mud-brick building to gradually disappear, ironically they had also played an unnoticed role in Fathy’s production of an Egyptian vernacular. Gharb Aswan, the village in which Fathy discovered an Egyptian architecture “preserved for centuries,” was in fact a modern village. It was built at the turn of the century to house people from the Nubian villages to the south, which were submerged by the reservoir created by the first Aswan Dam.

The dam had given Fathy the opportunity to build his vernacular village, by creating first the estates and then the epidemics that brought the politics of rural reconstruction into being. These irrigation works had simultaneously destroyed the country of Nubia, whose rebuilt houses were the inspiration for his Egyptian vernacular. The nation, and its heritage, must be made out of the material lives of others. In doing so, however, it incorporates processes and materials whose use and meaning it does not entirely control.
zh: 如果说阿斯旺的灌溉工程使土坯建筑逐渐消失，具有讽刺意味的是，它们也在法西制造埃及乡土风格的过程中扮演了未被注意的角色。西阿斯旺村——法西在其中发现了“保存数百年”的埃及建筑——实际上是一个现代村庄。它建于世纪之交，用来安置来自南部努比亚村庄的人；那些村庄被第一座阿斯旺大坝形成的水库淹没。
大坝先制造庄园、继而制造流行病，从而催生了乡村重建政治，给了法西建造其乡土村庄的机会。这些灌溉工程同时摧毁了努比亚人的家园，而努比亚重建的房屋正是他埃及乡土风格的灵感来源。民族及其传统，必须用他者的物质生活来制造。然而在这样做时，它纳入了一些过程和材料，而其用途和意义并不完全受它控制。

en: the performance of the past
zh: 过去的表演

en: Fifty years later the government was still trying to evict the population of old Gurna, and still describing them as lawless and unhygienic. To the old arguments about tomb robbing, official statements in the 1990s now added the claim that their “living conditions are poor, unhygienic, and spoil the view,” and that the presence of this large population in what was now recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site prevented its archaeological preservation and its development as an “open air museum.”
zh: 五十年后，政府仍在试图迁走旧古尔纳的居民，仍把他们描述为不守法、不卫生。除了关于盗墓的旧论调，1990年代的官方声明现在还增加了这样的说法：他们的“生活条件恶劣、不卫生，有碍景观”，而且这一大批人口身处如今已被联合国教科文组织认定为世界遗产的地点，妨碍了考古保护和将其发展为“露天博物馆”。

en: The issues were still those of heritage and civilization. But by the close of the twentieth century, Hassan Fathy’s vision of a national culture inspired by the revival of peasant initiative and know-how had disappeared, along with most of the houses of his model village. Instead the government planned an open-air museum, in which the role of the peasant, as we will see, was rather smaller. The development plans of the 1980s and 1990s are discussed more fully in the final section of this book. But the plans for the development of tourism and national heritage in Gurna can provide an introduction to these issues, as well as a contrast with the peasant politics of an earlier period.
zh: 问题仍然是传统与文明。但到20世纪末，哈桑·法西那种由复兴农民主动性和技能所激发的民族文化愿景已经消失，他模范村的大多数房屋也随之消失。政府转而规划了一座露天博物馆；正如我们将看到的，农民在其中的角色要小得多。本书最后一部分将更全面地讨论1980年代和1990年代的发展计划。但古尔纳旅游与民族传统发展的计划，可以为这些问题提供导论，并与早先时期的农民政治形成对照。

en: In 1982 the World Bank hired the U.S. consulting firm Arthur D. Little to draw up a program for increasing tourism revenue in Luxor (the same firm had been hired to do a similar study in 1953).

The consultants revived the proposal for the depopulation of Gurna, along with Hassan Fathy’s scheme to set up a cooperative to improve the quality of locally made souvenirs. With the local population removed, the increase in tourism revenue was to come from better “visitor management” and improved infrastructure to enable the development of luxury hotels and Nile cruise ships. Since there was a limit to the number of tourists who could be squeezed each hour in and out of King Tutankhamen’s tomb, income growth was to come partly from a shift toward wealthier tourists. The government proceeded to spend $60 million on these improvements, more than half of it borrowed from the World Bank to pay for foreign consultants and contractors.
zh: 1982年，世界银行聘请美国咨询公司阿瑟·D. 利特尔为卢克索制订一项增加旅游收入的计划（同一家公司曾在1953年受聘进行类似研究）。
咨询顾问重启了清空古尔纳居民的提议，以及哈桑·法西关于成立合作社以提高当地纪念品质量的想法。在迁走当地人口后，旅游收入的增长将来自更好的“游客管理”和改善的基础设施，以便发展豪华酒店和尼罗河游轮。由于每小时进出图坦卡蒙王陵的游客数量有限，收入增长部分要靠转向更富有的游客。政府随后在这些改善上花费6,000万美元，其中一半以上是从世界银行借来支付外国咨询顾问和承包商的。

en: These investments made possible a rapid growth in tourism. From 1982 to 1992 the number of visitors to Egypt and their estimated expenditures more than doubled (although attacks by Islamic militants caused numbers to dip again in the 1990s).

In Luxor most of the growth, as planned, was in luxury hotels and cruise ships. Across the river in Gurna, those who had established small hotels or other tourist enterprises before the development ban was imposed did well. They typically put their profits into importing small air-conditioned tour buses from Germany and Japan, or buying land and putting up apartment buildings in Luxor. For many villagers, however, there was almost no way of breaking into the tourist business, except for those who found unskilled work on the cruise ships at belowsubsistence wages. A few dozen young men did better by finding a foreign tourist to marry—usually a much older woman, who might visit each winter for a few weeks and with luck was wealthy enough to set the husband up in business. One woman, an enterprising California divorcée named Happy, began to build a small hotel on the edge of the desert south of the Theban Necropolis.

The building was stopped by the authorities, of course, and after six years and many payments to persuade the officials to allow construction to proceed the hotel was still not quite finished. Most of the husbands settled for something less, such as an imported car to run as a tourist taxi. Cruising past those working in the sugarcane fields in their air-conditioned Peugeots, these young men seemed to underline the separation of the tourist world from the village.
zh: 这些投资使旅游业得以快速增长。从1982年到1992年，前往埃及的游客人数及其估计支出增加了一倍以上（尽管伊斯兰武装分子的袭击使1990年代的人数再次下降）。

在卢克索，增长大多如计划那样出现在豪华酒店和游轮上。河对岸的古尔纳，那些在发展禁令实施前已经开办小旅馆或其他旅游企业的人做得不错。他们通常把利润用于从德国和日本进口小型空调旅游巴士，或在卢克索购买土地、建造公寓楼。然而，对许多村民来说，几乎没有办法进入旅游业，只有那些在游轮上找到低于生存工资的非技术工作的人例外。几十个年轻人则通过找外国游客结婚而过得好些——通常是一位年长许多的妇女，她可能每年冬天来访几周，若运气好，还有足够的钱让丈夫做生意。一位名叫哈皮的加州离婚妇女很有创业精神，开始在于底比斯墓地以南的沙漠边缘建造一座小旅馆。
当然，建筑被当局叫停；在六年和许多笔用于打通官员、使工程得以继续的款项之后，旅馆仍未完全完工。大多数丈夫只能满足于次一等的东西，比如一辆进口汽车用来跑旅游出租。这些年轻人开着空调标致车从甘蔗田里劳作的人身旁驶过，似乎凸显了旅游世界与村庄的分离。

en: The World Bank’s program was designed to increase this separation. Arthur D. Little, Inc., conducted a survey of tourists’ experiences in Luxor and reported, as they had in their 1953 study, that the biggest problem concerned the visitors’ contact with the local population. Tourists complained of being bothered continually by people trying to take them somewhere or sell them something. The consultants recommended that no further peddlers’ licenses be issued.
zh: 世界银行的计划旨在加剧这种分离。阿瑟·D. 利特尔公司对游客在卢克索的体验进行了调查，并像其1953年的研究一样报告说，最大的问题在于游客与当地人口的接触。游客抱怨不断被人打扰，有人想带他们去什么地方，有人想卖东西给他们。咨询顾问建议不再发放小贩执照。

en: More significantly, the visitor management scheme they devised was planned to minimize unregulated contact with the tourists and increase their physical separation from the local community. Separate river ferry and bus facilities were developed to isolate the movement of tourists from local traffic. An enclosed visitor center with its own restaurant and shops was to be built to enclose the tourists waiting for transportation. In a village adjacent to Gurna the plans called for an elevated walkway to be erected through the middle of the hamlet, so that tourists could cross from the bus parking lot to the Pharaonic temple without touching the village itself.
zh: 更重要的是，他们设计的游客管理方案旨在尽量减少与游客不受管制的接触，并加大游客与当地社区的身体隔离。他们开发了单独的渡河轮渡和巴士设施，使游客的流动与本地交通相隔绝。计划建造一座封闭的游客中心，内有餐厅和商店，把等待交通工具的游客围在其中。在与古尔纳相邻的一个村庄，计划要求在小村中央架设一条高架步道，使游客可以从巴士停车场走到法老神庙，而不接触村庄本身。

en: Enclave tourism, as this kind of arrangement is called, had become the typical pattern of tourist development in regions outside Europe and North America. It appeared to be required by the increasing disparity between the wealth of the tourists and the poverty of those whose countries they visited. The Egyptian Ministry of Tourism appealed to foreign capitalists considering putting money into hotels or other tourist enterprises in Egypt with the claim that investors were “enjoying outstanding profits in the tourism field,” thanks to the easy repatriation of those profits and to “labor costs that are more than competitive on a world-wide scale.”

In the late 1980s the ministry calculated that each tourist spent on average $100 a day in Egypt, which was more than most hotel employees earned in a month. A decade later the disparity was far greater.
The difference in wealth was so pronounced that the tourists’ enjoyment could only be secured by their physical separation from the host community.
zh: 这种安排被称为“飞地旅游”，已成为欧洲和北美以外地区旅游开发的典型模式。游客的财富与他们所访问国家人民的贫困之间日益扩大的差距，似乎使这种模式成为必需。埃及旅游部向考虑投资埃及酒店或其他旅游企业的外国资本家宣传说，投资者“在旅游领域享有丰厚利润”，这得益于利润的便捷汇出以及“在全球范围内极具竞争力的劳动力成本”。
1980年代后期，旅游部估算每位游客在埃及平均每天花费100美元，超过大多数酒店雇员一个月的收入。十年后，差距更大。
财富差异如此悬殊，只有让游客与东道主社区身体隔离，才能保障游客的享受。

en: There was a further reason for the creation of enclave tourism. As the industry became concentrated in the hands of luxury hotels under the management of U.S.- or European-based international chains, along with half a dozen large Egyptian entrepreneurs, the hotel managers sought to increase their profits by containing more tourist expenditure within their own establishments.

The grand Egyptian hotels that used to provide little more than spacious accommodations and an elegant dining room were replaced by hotel complexes that offered three or four different restaurants and cuisines, several bars, shopping arcades, a swimming pool and fitness club, cruises and excursions, business facilities, and evening lectures and entertainment. The Nile cruise ships and the walled “tourist villages” popular where space was plentiful, such as the Red Sea coast, were even more self-contained.
zh: 建立飞地旅游还有另一个原因。随着该行业集中到由欧美跨国公司管理的豪华酒店以及六家埃及大企业手中，酒店管理者力求通过把更多游客支出留在自己的场所内来增加利润。
过去只提供宽敞客房和雅致餐厅的埃及大酒店，被酒店综合体取代；后者提供三四种不同餐馆和菜系、数个酒吧、购物拱廊、游泳池和健身俱乐部、游轮和短途旅行、商务设施，以及晚间讲座和娱乐。尼罗河游轮和在空间充裕之处（如红海海岸）流行的有围墙的“旅游村”，则更为自给自足。

en: In chapter 2 we encountered a different kind of walled village, the ʿizba or housing complex built for the workers on large agricultural estates. There is no similarity between the two kinds of enclosures, except this: both represent methods to contain a population, to establish a local zone of sovereignty where external forms of law, exchange, or movement might not apply. In a later chapter we will consider how what is called capitalism or the market adopts many different strategies to build enclosures or enclaves of this sort.
zh: 在第2章，我们遇到过另一种有围墙的村庄，即伊兹巴，也就是大型农业庄园为工人建造的住宅群。这两种围合体之间没有相似之处，只有一点例外：二者都代表着容纳人口的方法，即建立一个地方主权区域，在那里，外部的法律、交换或流动形式可能不适用。在后面的章节中，我们将考察所谓的资本主义或市场如何采用多种不同策略来建造这类围合体或飞地。

en: If the ʿizba was built to keep the peasants in, the enclave hotel was built to keep them out. The local population, except for a small elite, was excluded by the prices charged and the guards posted at the gate. To enter particular areas, such as the swimming pool or gambling casino, a foreign passport might be required. The result was a system of almost total segregation. Most Luxor tourists found themselves living, eating, and sleeping in their enclave hotels, traveling in separate air-conditioned taxis and buses, and going to separate entertainments. The few occasions in which organized tourists encountered the local street, whether half an hour set aside for shopping in the Luxor bazaar or a five-minute walk from the cruise ship to an archaeological site through a strip of village, became frenzied scenes in which local peddlers, merchants, and entrepreneurs tried to secure some small share of the tourist business.
zh: 如果说伊兹巴建来是为了把农民关在里面，那么飞地酒店建来则是为了把他们挡在外面。除一小部分精英外，当地人口被收取的价格和门口的警卫排除在外。要进入游泳池或赌场等特定区域，可能需要外国护照。结果是几乎完全隔离的制度。大多数卢克索游客发现自己在那飞地酒店里起居、饮食、睡觉，乘坐单独的空调出租车和巴士，参加单独的娱乐活动。有组织的游客与当地街道接触的少数场合——无论是在卢克索集市留出半小时购物，还是从游轮穿过一片村庄步行五分钟到考古遗址——都变成了狂乱的场面，当地小贩、商人和创业者试图从中分得旅游业的一小杯羹。

en: The segregation was further encouraged by government and World Bank policy. In the 1980s the World Bank directed Egyptian public funds into building the infrastructure for tourist development. In the 1990s the World Bank pushed for the profits from this public investment to be switched into private Egyptian and foreign hands. Supported by a former IMF employee and banker–turned–minister of tourism, Fuʾad Sultan, in 1992 the World Bank paid the consultants Coopers and Lybrand Deloitte to draw up plans to sell off the country’s luxury hotels, which, although managed by international hotel chains, were still owned by the state.

The hotels were highly profitable, providing returns of up to 50 percent of revenue or more. As the consultants acknowledged, the investors enjoyed prospects for windfall profits from the future resale of undervalued properties.
zh: 政府和世界银行的政策进一步鼓励了隔离。1980年代，世界银行引导埃及公共资金建设旅游开发的基础设施。1990年代，世界银行推动把这项公共投资的利润转入埃及和外国私人手中。在前国际货币基金组织雇员、银行家出身的旅游部长福阿德·苏丹的支持下，世界银行于1992年聘请咨询公司库珀斯与莱布兰德·德勤制订计划，出售该国豪华酒店：这些酒店虽由国际酒店连锁管理，仍为国家所有。
酒店利润丰厚，回报率高达收入的50%甚至更多。正如咨询顾问所承认的，投资者享有从未来转售被低估资产中获取暴利的前景。

en: Whatever the windfall, the increased control of Luxor tourism by outside capital had two likely consequences. First, it would send not just the profits from tourism abroad, but tourist expenditure in general. Increasing international integration of the tourist industry decreases the proportion of tourist expenditure that remains in the host country or region.
The integration of the hotel industry was accompanied in the 1990s by that of the foreign tour operators.

Second, as those who purchased these assets increased the pressure on local managers to build their share of a limited market, the process of segregating the tourists within their luxury enclaves would intensify. For the young men of Gurna and neighboring villages seeking employment, both developments were likely to decrease the proportion of tourism income available to the local community.
zh: 无论暴利如何，外部资本对卢克索旅游业控制的加强可能带来两个后果。第一，它不仅会把旅游利润送往国外，也会把一般的旅游支出送往国外。旅游业日益国际化的一体化，降低了留在东道国或地区的旅游支出比例。
1990年代，酒店业的一体化伴随着外国旅游运营商的一体化。
第二，随着购买这些资产的人加大对当地管理者的压力、要求在一个有限市场中分得自己的份额，把游客隔离在豪华飞地内的进程将会加剧。对于古尔纳及邻近村庄寻找工作的年轻人来说，这两种发展都可能减少当地社区可获得的旅游收入比例。

en: Yet even as the process of segregation developed, the lives of the local community were increasingly affected by the tourist presence. Because of the kind of industry tourism is, its development involves more than a simple process of segregation. A conventional industry, whether based in manufacturing or agriculture, involves organizing people to produce. Mass production relies upon all the well-known methods of recruiting and disciplining a workforce, organizing their use of time, their movement, and their arrangement in physical space, and developing systems of instruction, supervision, and management. Mass tourism, by contrast, involves organizing people to consume. It relies upon similar methods of managing flows and timetables, arranging physical space, and instructing and supervising, to maximize the process of consumption.
zh: 然而，即便隔离进程不断发展，当地社区的生活仍越来越受到游客存在的影响。由于旅游业这种产业的性质，其发展涉及的不仅仅是简单的隔离过程。传统产业，无论是制造业还是农业，都涉及组织人们生产。批量生产依赖所有众所周知的方法：招募和规训劳动力，组织他们对时间的使用、他们的流动以及他们在物理空间中的安排，并发展指导、监督和管理系统。相比之下，大众旅游涉及组织人们消费。它依赖类似的方法——管理流量和时间表、安排物理空间、指导与监督——以最大化消费过程。

en: Tourism is an industry of consumption, and the consumption not of individual goods but of a more complex commodity, experiences. No object of modern consumption is ever just a thing. The purchase of food, clothing, or cars is always the purchase of a certain taste, lifestyle, or experience. One pays not just for the thing but for what it signifies. With tourism, this consumption of what things signify is taken to the extreme. The tourist industry sells not individual objects of signification but entire worlds of experience and meaning.
zh: 旅游业是一种消费产业，消费的不是单个物品，而是一种更复杂的商品——体验。现代消费的对象从来不只是物品。购买食物、衣物或汽车，总是购买某种品味、生活方式或体验。人们不仅为物品付钱，也为它所象征的东西付钱。在旅游业中，这种对物品所象征之物的消费被推向极致。旅游产业出售的不是单个象征物，而是整个体验与意义的世界。

en: In Luxor the tourism industry marketed the consumption of ancient Egypt. The experience was created out of the archaeological sites, but also by organizing the contemporary society to appear as a reflection and extension of the past. The 1982 World Bank report on visitor management explained that “the creation of an overall environment is needed on the West Bank in order for Luxor to reach its full market potential.”

This meant turning Gurna into an “open air museum,” its population moved out, and its houses destroyed. A few houses were to be left standing as examples of local architecture, and used to house artisans and craftsmen producing tourist artifacts.
zh: 在卢克索，旅游产业营销的是对古埃及的消费。这种体验不仅由考古遗址创造，也通过把当代社会组织得看起来像是过去的反映和延伸来创造。世界银行1982年关于游客管理的报告解释说，“西岸需要营造一个整体环境，卢克索才能充分发挥其市场潜力。”
这意味着把古尔纳变成一座“露天博物馆”，迁走居民，摧毁房屋。少数房屋将保留下来，作为当地建筑的范例，并用于安置制作旅游工艺品的工匠艺人。

en: The new plans to evict the population of Gurna were formalized in a study carried out between 1992 and 1994. The new relocation site, first identified and surveyed in the 1950s, lay several kilometers to the north. Adopting themes first articulated by Hassan Fathy and subsequently transformed into standard development practice, the Terms of Reference for the relocation study, funded by USAID, emphasized the need for detailed architectural, social, and cultural surveys of the old village and “community participation” in the planning. The former now involved the making of an ethnographic film about the community that was to be removed, while “community participation” was reduced to constructing plywood model houses in three sizes, which villagers could visit to select their house design.

Several hundred villagers, in most cases those who were able to exchange one old house for several new ones, agreed to move to the new settlements, leading to extreme overcrowding (since 1978 the government had banned further building in old Gurna). So only a few dozen old houses were available for demolition. When the government tried to force other villagers to move, the result more than once was resistance, culminating in the riot and shootings of January 1998.
zh: 迁走古尔纳居民的新计划在1992至1994年间进行的一项研究中正式确定。新的安置地点最早在1950年代被确认和测量，位于以北几公里处。搬迁研究的职权范围由美国国际开发署资助，采用了哈桑·法西最早阐述、后来转化为标准发展实践的主题，强调需要对旧村进行详细的建筑、社会和文化调查，并在规划中实行“社区参与”。前者此时变成拍摄一部关于即将迁走之共同体的人种志影片，而“社区参与”则被简化为建造三种尺寸的胶合板房屋模型，供村民参观并选择自己的房屋设计。
几百名村民同意迁往新定居点，他们大多是能够用一栋旧房换几栋新房的人，这导致极度拥挤（自1978年以来，政府禁止在旧古尔纳继续建房）。因此只有几十栋旧房可供拆除。当政府试图强迫其他村民搬迁时，不止一次遇到抵抗，最终酿成1998年1月的骚乱和枪击。

en: The World Bank, USAID, and the Egyptian Government spent tens of millions of dollars during the 1990s alone planning and attempting once again the eviction of the people of Gurna.

Despite this large employment of architects, planners, ethnographers, bureaucrats, and bulldozers, there was little investigation of the actual need for the evictions or their possible impact. While there were studies of the aesthetics and culture of old Gurna, there was to be no investigation of the actual problems these people were said to be creating, which might put in question the need for the evictions and for the employment of so much expertise.
zh: 仅1990年代，世界银行、美国国际开发署和埃及政府就花费数千万美元，规划并再次尝试迁走古尔纳的人民。
尽管大量动用建筑师、规划师、人种志学者、官僚和推土机，却几乎没有调查驱逐的实际需要或其可能影响。虽然有对旧古尔纳美学和文化的研究，却没有调查这些人据说正在造成的实际问题；这种调查可能会质疑驱逐的必要性，以及动用如此多专业知识的必要性。

en: The alleged problems can be briefly examined. First, it was said, the people of Gurna were tomb robbers, an accusation repeated so often that even many critics of the eviction assumed it to be true. The image of tomb robbers was a standard element in national media representations of Gurna, from Shadi ʿAbd al-Salam’s famous film of 1969, al-Mumiya (The Mummy), to a popular television serial aired during the middle of theses events in 1996–97, Hilm al-janubi (The Southerner’s Dream), whose plot turned on the conflict between an evil tomb robber in the Luxor area and an educated hero who sought to defend and rediscover Egypt’s heritage.

Occasionally the government reinforced these images by staging a raid on a Gurna house. In 1996 Muhammad al-Adhim, sixty-three years old, came home to find that the authorities had discovered a tomb cut into the rock behind the wall of his late great-grandmother’s bedroom. The tomb was just an empty tunnel, but this did not stop the authorities from arresting the old man, who worked as an assistant in a local dentist’s office, and making a public example of him. “I am completely stunned. I never knew there was a tunnel,” he said. “I think the tourist authority just made a balloon to attract foreigners. Tomorrow they will say these slippers I am wearing came from Ramses II.” Tomb robbers, he pointed out, were supposed to make lots of money. “But can you tell me where is my Mercedes, where is my six-storey house?”
