zh: 可以对据称的问题作简要考察。首先，据说古尔纳人是盗墓贼；这一指控被反复传播，以致连许多反对驱逐的人也假定它是真的。盗墓贼的形象是国家媒体再现古尔纳的标准元素，从沙迪·阿卜杜勒-萨拉姆1969年的著名电影《木乃伊》（al-Mumiya），到1996—1997年这些事件进行期间播出的热门电视剧《南方人之梦》（Hilm al-janubi）；后者的情节围绕卢克索地区一个邪恶盗墓贼与一位试图捍卫和重新发现埃及遗产的受过教育的英雄之间的冲突展开。

政府偶尔通过安排突袭古尔纳一处民宅来强化这些形象。1996年，六十三岁的穆罕默德·阿齐姆回到家，发现当局在他已故曾祖母卧室墙壁后的岩石中发现了一座凿出的坟墓。那座墓只是一条空隧道，但这并未阻止当局逮捕这位在当地牙医诊所当助理的老人，并把他当作公开的反面典型。“我完全惊呆了。我从来不知道那里有条隧道，”他说。“我想旅游局只是为了吸引外国人放了个气球。明天他们就会说我脚上这双拖鞋来自拉美西斯二世。”他指出，盗墓贼本应赚很多钱。“可你能告诉我，我的奔驰在哪里，我那六层楼的房子在哪里吗？”

en: Over some two hundred years certain households in Gurna formed a small part of the international network that moved the treasures of ancient Egypt to the great museums and private collections of Europe and North America. It is curious that we now look back on the Gurnawis as tomb robbers, but still find it difficult to describe the British Museum in London or the Metropolitan Museum in New York as collections of stolen goods.

An illicit trade in Egyptian antiquities still continued, driven by the demand from private collectors in the West. Occasionally these trading rings were broken, however, and news reports showed that the sources of stolen goods were invariably storerooms under the control of the government, dozens of which were dotted around the country, holding as many as a million pieces.

These problems might have best been addressed by measures such as better pay and training for local employees of the antiquities authority, more secure storerooms, and a more vigorous international campaign against the American and European dealers. In 1970 UNESCO adopted a convention to prohibit and prevent the international trade in stolen art and antiquities. Thirty years later, Britain, Germany, Switzerland, Japan, and several other countries that played an important role in the illegal trade had not ratified the convention.
Enforcement was so weak that Interpol estimated that 90 to 95 percent of stolen artifacts were never recovered.
Attempts to get the United States and other leading importers of stolen antiquities to pass domestic legislation to prevent the trade were also unsuccessful.

It was easier to demand the eviction of villagers from a hillside in southern Egypt than to investigate how the trade in antiquities was actually organized and run and to collaborate on measures against international dealers and buyers. Development agencies, architects, planners, and academics could then repeat without evidence the claim that Gurnawis were tomb robbers.
zh: 大约两百年来，古尔纳的某些家庭构成了一个国际网络的一小部分；这个网络把古埃及的珍宝运往欧洲和北美的大博物馆与私人收藏。奇怪的是，我们如今把古尔纳人追溯为盗墓贼，却仍然难以把伦敦大英博物馆或纽约大都会博物馆描述为赃物收藏。
埃及文物的非法交易仍在继续，其驱动力是西方私人收藏家的需求。然而，这些交易圈偶尔会被破获，新闻报道表明，赃物的来源无一例外都是政府控制的库房；全国散布着几十座这样的库房，藏品多达一百万件。
这些问题本来最好通过以下措施解决：提高文物局当地雇员的薪酬和培训，加强库房安全，以及更有力地开展针对美国和欧洲交易商的国际运动。1970年，联合国教科文组织通过了一项公约，禁止和防止被盗艺术品和文物的国际交易。三十年后，英国、德国、瑞士、日本以及其他几个在非法交易中起重要作用的国家仍未批准该公约。
执法如此薄弱，以致国际刑警组织估计90%至95%的被盗文物从未追回。
促使美国和其他被盗文物主要进口国通过国内立法防止交易的尝试也未成功。
要求把村民从埃及南部一片山坡上迁走，要比调查文物交易实际上如何组织和运作、并合作采取措施打击国际交易商和买家容易得多。于是，发展机构、建筑师、规划师和学者可以毫无证据地重复古尔纳人是盗墓贼的说法。

en: Second, it was argued, whether or not they were robbing its tombs, the villagers of Gurna were damaging the Theban Necropolis by their very presence. The wastewater from the Gurna houses was damaging the tombs, the authorities claimed, and houses built over tombs “spoiled the view” and prevented the development of tourism.
zh: 第二，有人争辩说，无论古尔纳村民是否盗掘陵墓，他们的存在本身就损害了底比斯墓地。当局声称，古尔纳房屋的废水正在损坏陵墓，而建在陵墓上的房屋“有碍景观”，妨碍旅游开发。

en: Again, it is not clear what the evidence was for these claims. The hamlets of Gurna were not allowed to have running water or to dig wells. They had to fetch all the water they needed in wheeled oil drums pulled by donkey. The only running water on the Theban hillside was in the accommodations of the European archaeological missions. Although moisture damage was a serious problem, there was no geological survey of the Gurna site, with its alternating layers of limestone and shale, to assess the impact of habitation (versus, for example, the impact of the general raising of the water table and humidity levels since the building of the Aswan High Dam), or to identify which locations could support human occupation without damage to the tombs.

Once again, despite the millions of dollars spent on outside consultants, these basic studies had not been done. Nor was any effort made to consider less disruptive solutions to the problem of wastewater.
zh: 同样不清楚这些说法有何证据。古尔纳的小村不被允许接通自来水或打井。他们必须用驴拉的带轮油桶运回所需的所有用水。底比斯山坡上唯一的自来水在欧洲考古队的住所里。尽管湿气损害是一个严重问题，却没有对古尔纳遗址（石灰岩与页岩交替的岩层）进行地质调查，以评估居住的影响（例如与阿斯旺高坝建成以来地下水位和湿度总体上升的影响相较），或确定哪些地点可以容纳人类居住而不损害陵墓。
再一次，尽管花费数百万美元聘请外部咨询顾问，这些基础研究却没有做。也没有任何努力去考虑对废水问题破坏性更小的解决办法。

en: Detailed information was available, on the other hand, about the damage that tourists were doing, and especially the damage done by tourists’ wastewater. If a tomb in the Theban Necropolis was occupied by twelve visitors, in one hour their sweat increased the relative humidity by 5 percent. At the peak of the tourist season, up to 4,500 tourists visited the Necropolis every hour. More than one-third of them, between 1,500 and 2,000, visited the three most popular tombs, causing the humidity in them to increase by up to 100 percent, a level at which one-fifth of the wall painting can be lost.

Although villagers could be denied running water to reduce the problem of wastewater, there appeared to be no equivalent way to stop tourists from sweating. The master plan for Luxor, of which the depopulation of Gurna was a part, envisioned quadrupling the number of tourists within twenty years, from one million each year to four million. Every one of those three million extra visitors would want to squeeze themselves, dripping with perspiration, into and out of the tombs of Gurna. Far from eliminating the problem of wastewater, the plans for Gurna were going to add to it significantly.
zh: 另一方面，关于游客造成的损害，尤其是游客废水造成的损害，却有详细资料。如果底比斯墓地的一座陵墓一次进入十二名参观者，他们的汗水在一小时内会使相对湿度上升5%。旅游旺季，每小时多达4,500名游客参观墓地。其中三分之一以上——1,500至2,000人——参观三个最热门的陵墓，使其湿度最多上升100%；达到这一水平时，壁画的五分之一可能损毁。
虽然可以通过不给村民供应自来水来减少废水问题，却似乎没有相应的办法阻止游客出汗。卢克索总体规划（清空古尔纳是其中一部分）设想在二十年内把游客人数增加三倍，从每年一百万增至四百万。新增的三百万游客中的每一个人，都想汗淋淋地挤进挤出古尔纳的陵墓。古尔纳计划远未消除废水问题，反而会大大加剧这个问题。

en: As for access to the ancient tombs, although a handful of them had houses built over their entrances, there were many hundreds of others that were not concealed by houses yet were not opened up to tourism. Some of these were used by the authorities for other purposes, such as storerooms. The tombs concealed by the houses the authorities wanted to demolish were arguably better off than all the rest. Although tombs of no archaeological significance were often simply cavelike extensions of the house built against them, the few of archaeological merit were closed off from the house itself and controlled by the antiquities department. Moreover, the relationship between household and tomb may represent a more historically interesting aspect of the local heritage than many of the empty tombs cleared out and opened up as tourist sites. Indeed, one or two archaeologists working in the area had started to dig not in uncleared tombs but in the piles of debris cleared out by earlier excavations. Earlier excavators were interested only in Pharaonic treasure, or at most in the art and artifacts of the Pharaonic period. Yet many of the tombs came to serve as human habitations over subsequent centuries, and the debris of earlier excavations contains rich evidence of this long period of Coptic and early Islamic local life. The communities living among the tombs today may date back a mere four or five hundred years. But as van der Spek argues, the relationship they represent between a dead past and a living community is part of the history of the Theban Necropolis.
zh: 至于通往古代陵墓的入口，虽然少数陵墓的入口上方建有房屋，但还有数百座陵墓并未被房屋遮挡，却也没有向旅游业开放。其中一些被当局用于其他目的，例如库房。当局想要拆除的房屋所遮蔽的陵墓，可以说比其余所有陵墓境况更好。虽然没有考古意义的陵墓往往只是在房屋边上扩展出的洞穴状空间，但少数有考古价值的陵墓与房屋本身隔开，并由文物部门控制。此外，家户与陵墓之间的关系，可能是当地传统中比许多被清理出来、作为旅游景点开放的空墓更有历史趣味的方面。事实上，在这一地区工作的一两位考古学家已经开始挖掘的不是未清理的陵墓，而是早期发掘清理出的碎石堆。早期发掘者只对法老时代的珍宝感兴趣，最多对法老时期的艺术和器物感兴趣。然而，许多陵墓在此后数世纪中成为人的居所，早期发掘的碎石中含有科普特和早期伊斯兰时期当地生活这一漫长阶段的丰富证据。今天生活在陵墓之间的共同体或许只能追溯四五百年。但正如范德施佩克所主张的，它们所代表的死去的过去与活着的共同体之间的关系，是底比斯墓地历史的一部分。

en: In 1981 half a million tourists visited Luxor and each stayed for an average of only 2.1 nights. By the 1990s the number of visitors in a good year was more than double that, but the length of stay had declined to an average of less than one night.

The local tourist industry had less than twenty-four hours within which to maximize the tourist’s consumption. This required a meticulous planning of meals, drinks, sleeping, and entertainment, as well as the requisite trips to Karnak and Luxor temples, the sound and light show, the felucca ride, a visit to the Luxor bazaar, plus trips to King Tutankhamen’s tomb and other sundry tombs and temples of the Theban Necropolis across the river.
zh: 1981年，五十万游客访问卢克索，平均每人只停留2.1夜。到1990年代，好年景的游客人数是其两倍多，但停留时间已下降到平均不到一夜。
当地旅游业在不到二十四小时里要尽可能扩大游客的消费。这需要精心安排餐饮、睡眠和娱乐，以及必不可少的卡纳克和卢克索神庙之行、声光表演、帆船游览、卢克索集市，外加图坦卡蒙王陵和河对岸底比斯墓地其他各类陵墓神庙。

en: This mass production of experience produced a curious common interest between tourism’s overorganized heritage consumers and some of the local community. In the 1982 World Bank survey, alongside the complaint about the behavior of peddlers and local merchants, the most frequent tourist request was for more meaningful contact with the local population. Many tourists to Luxor were anxious to escape the routine and meet “real Egyptians.” Many of the local population, interested in diverting tourist expenditure back toward their own needs, were keen to help. Zaynab, for example, had a house directly in front of a parking area for tour buses. Her children would hang around the buses, out of sight of the tour guides, and catch the eye of tourists lagging behind the main group as it headed off toward the temple. They then invited them into the house to watch their mother baking bread at the earthen oven. The children expected a tip of a pound or so, and some of the tourists even offered money to their mother.
zh: 这种体验的大批量生产，在旅游业的过度组织化遗产消费者与部分当地社区之间，产生了一种奇特的共同利益。在世界银行1982年的调查中，除了对小贩和当地商人行为的抱怨之外，游客最常提出的要求是希望与当地人口有更有意义的接触。许多到卢克索的游客渴望逃离常规，见到“真正的埃及人”。许多当地人则想把游客支出导回自身需求，因而乐于帮忙。例如，扎伊纳布的家就在旅游巴士停车场正前方。她的孩子们会在巴士周围徘徊，避开导游的视线，吸引那些在主队前往神庙时落在后面的游客。然后他们邀请游客进屋，看母亲在地灶里烤面包。孩子们期待一镑左右的小费，有些游客甚至给他们的母亲塞钱。

en: The mass consumption of heritage included countless small encounters of this sort, in which the logics of exclusion, impoverishment, and eviction were briefly suspended. Such events operated like a local ecotourism, almost invisible to the large-scale tourist industry, performing, like Zaynab’s children, behind its back, yet for many individual tourists often representing the highlight of their day, far more memorable than all that sweaty Theban heritage. These encounters very occasionally developed into longer exchanges, including the foreign women who as tourists found a part-time husband in the village. None of this was necessarily an ecotourism to celebrate, for it was usually constructed on considerable inequalities and misunderstandings. But it does remind us that the manufacture and consumption of heritage produced encounters beyond the control of heritage managers, where the act of consumption briefly undermined the place of things in the heritage system.
zh: 遗产的大众消费包括无数此类小小遭遇，在这些遭遇中，排斥、贫困化和驱逐的逻辑暂时中止。这类事件像是一种本地生态旅游，几乎不被大型旅游产业看见，像扎伊纳布的孩子们一样在它背后进行；然而对许多个体游客来说，它们往往是当天的亮点，比所有那些汗淋淋的底比斯遗产更令人难忘。这类遭遇偶尔会发展为更长期的交往，包括一些作为游客的外国妇女在村里找到了兼职丈夫。这一切不一定值得庆祝为生态旅游，因为它通常建立在相当程度的不平等和误解之上。但它确实提醒我们，遗产的制造和消费产生了不受遗产管理者控制的遭遇；在那些遭遇中，消费行为短暂地动摇了事物在遗产体系中的位置。

en: Let me conclude by bringing the question of tourism and the heritage industry back to the issue of producing the nation. In November 1996, the heads of more than seventy Gurna households threatened with eviction and the demolition of their homes signed a petition to the authorities. “We the people of Gurna,” it stated,
zh: 最后，让我把旅游和遗产产业的问题带回制造民族这一主题。1996年11月，古尔纳七十多户面临驱逐和房屋拆除的家庭的户主向当局签署了一份请愿书。请愿书声称：“我们古尔纳人民

en: . . . have become threatened in our homes, we have become agonized with fear, while our houses are demolished above our heads and we are driven from our homeland. Sirs, you know the feelings suffered by the refugee driven from his home, the exile from his land, the person who becomes a stranger in his own country. We have begun to wonder whether we are Egyptians.
zh: ……在自己的家中受到威胁，我们在恐惧中煎熬，房屋在我们头顶被拆毁，我们被逐出家园。先生们，你们知道被赶出家的难民、被逐出故土的流亡者、在自己国家成为陌生人的人所受的感受。我们开始怀疑自己是不是埃及人。

en: The petition describes the fear and violence of relocation, connecting it to other, more brutal expulsions of a sort that Egyptians in recent history have not had to face. The villagers then invoke for themselves the idea of the nation, asking the question “whether we are Egyptians.” This simple question opens up the contradictions of nation making. Their eviction has been justified as a project of producing the nation. To preserve the heritage of the nation, and to turn those portrayed as lawless and uneducated into honest citizens of the state, they must be expelled from their homes. To produce the nation requires an act of violence, and in revealing this violence its victims bring to light the forces and instabilities that nation making brings into play. The petition continues:
zh: 请愿书描述了搬迁的恐惧和暴力，把它与其他更残酷的驱逐联系起来——那种埃及人在近代史上不曾不得不面对的事情。随后，村民为自己援引民族的观念，提出“我们是不是埃及人”的问题。这个简单的问题揭示了造就民族的矛盾。他们的驱逐一直以制造民族的项目为理由。为了保存民族的传统，并把那些被描绘为不守法、未受教育的人变成国家的诚实公民，他们必须被逐出家园。制造民族需要一次暴力行为，而受害者在揭示这种暴力时，也揭示了造就民族所动用的力量和不稳定因素。请愿书继续写道：

en: The pretext for all this is that we damage and do harm to tourism and that we threaten the safety of the monuments. We do not understand who has fabricated these rumors. We come from the monuments and by the monuments we exist. Our livelihood is from tourism. We have no source of sustenance beyond God except for our work with tourism. . . . We are married to the tourists.
zh: 这一切的借口是我们损害和妨害旅游业，我们威胁纪念物的安全。我们不明白是谁编造了这些谣言。我们来自这些纪念物，靠这些纪念物生存。我们的生计来自旅游业。除了上帝，我们除了从事旅游业的工作之外没有别的生计来源……我们与游客结了婚。

en: Against the popular official portrayal of them as backward, unclean, ignorant, and an obstacle to the development of a modern heritage site, they declare “we are married to the tourists.” Both a metaphor for their close involvement with the tourist industry, and a reference to the fact that foreign women have in fact married local men, this claim gently but insistently subverts the official rhetoric.
zh: 面对官方流行的描绘——落后、不洁、无知、阻碍现代遗产地发展的障碍——他们宣称“我们与游客结了婚”。这一说法既隐喻他们与旅游业的密切联系，也指外国妇女确实嫁给了当地男子这一事实，温和而坚持地颠覆了官方修辞。

en: Given that the authorities had been periodically attempting to evict the people of Gurna for more than five decades, and now had on their side all the resources of bulldozers, armed police forces, tourism investors, and U.S. and World Bank consultants, it is important to take seriously the power to subvert the violent plans of the heritage industry. This subversion, I have argued, was not the pure resistance of an indigenous community opposed to the plans of the authorities. It was a subversion that operated within, and opened up to view, the contradictions of the projects of heritage and nation making. The manufacturing of a national heritage attempted to divide the world into consumers of tradition and the dead, depopulated heritage they were to consume. But on numerous levels and in multiple ways, neither the consumers nor those facing eviction agreed to this program. And in their minor acts of disruption, they brought its hidden violence into view.
zh: 鉴于当局五十多年来一直周期性地试图迁走古尔纳人民，如今又拥有推土机、武装警察、旅游投资者以及美国和世界银行咨询顾问等一切资源，认真对待颠覆遗产产业暴力计划的力量就很重要。我曾论证，这种颠覆不是原住民共同体对当局计划的纯粹抵抗。它是一种在遗产和民族制造工程的矛盾内部运作、并使这些矛盾显露出来的颠覆。民族传统的制造试图把世界划分为传统的消费者和供他们消费的、死去的、清空了人的遗产。但在许多层面，以多种方式，无论是消费者还是面临驱逐的人，都不认同这一方案。而他们小小的扰乱行为，使其中隐藏的暴力显露出来。

en: Fathy was educated in British schools in Cairo. In 1956, with the collapse of the European presence in Egypt following the failed British, French, and Israeli invasion that year, he chose to leave Egypt himself and spent the next five years based in Athens. Thus he abandoned Egypt at the moment of triumph of an alternative vision of national heritage, that of Arab nationalism. Architecture for the Poor was translated into Arabic only in the 1980s. See Steele, An Architecture for the People, 96, 109. On the problems of Fathy’s cosmopolitanism see Nezar AlSayyad,“From Vernacularism to Globalism:The Temporal Reality of Traditional Settlements,” Traditional Dwellings and Settlements Review 7, no. 1 (1995): 13–24. Fathy’s cosmopolitanism, however, may have been central to his achievement. Perhaps it gave him a certain distance from the narrower materialism and less generous paternalism of the landowning class from which he came, and opened him to the influence of other inventions of the modern vernacular, such as French colonial architecture in Morocco. For example, the Habous neighborhood built in the late 1930s in Casablanca, and copied some years later in Rabat, was widely discussed in this period as a reaction against the modernist movement and Le Corbusier (Muhammed Hamdouni Alami, personal communication, Feb. 10, 1999).

en: The local method consisted of building a parallel series of mud-brick arches, set about an arm’s length apart. The gaps between them were filled with a thick mud plaster mixed with a large amount of straw, laid up by hand working in circular fashion (tuuf) from the edges towards the center, as though making an inverted clay bowl. (Indeed, tuuf was typically a woman’s skill, used for making large bowls and the domed roofs of bread ovens and grain silos.) The resulting vault was quite shallow, but strong enough to allow another floor to be built above—another advantage over Fathy’s more highly arched method, which, like the dome, did not easily allow the later addition of an upper floor. Nessim Henry Henein, Ma ̄rı ̄ Girgis: Village de Haute-Egypte (Cairo: Institut français d’archéologie orientale du Caire, 1988), 40–41, 49; Boutros Wadieh, personal communication, Jan. 2001.
zh: 这种本地方法包括建造一系列平行的土坯拱，彼此相隔约一臂长。拱之间的空隙用手工制作的厚泥灰填充，泥灰混有大量稻草，从边缘向中心以圆形方式（tuuf）堆砌，就像制作倒扣的泥碗。（事实上，tuuf 通常是妇女的技能，用于制作大碗以及面包炉和粮仓的穹顶。）形成的拱顶相当浅，但足以在其上再建一层楼——这比法西那种高高拱起的方法（与穹顶一样，不易日后加建上层）又多了一个优点。Nessim Henry Henein, Mārī Girgis: Village de Haute-Egypte (Cairo: Institut français d’archéologie orientale du Caire, 1988), 40–41, 49; Boutros Wadieh, personal communication, Jan. 2001.
